articles.title: Asian Para Games: Praveen Kumar clinches gold in high jump T64, Unni Renu gets bronze
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Indian para-athletes Praveen Kumar and Unni Renu achieved a remarkable double podium finish in the men's high jump event of the Asian Para Games in Ha
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-athletes Praveen Kumar and Unni Renu achieved a remarkable double podium finish in the men's high jump event of the Asian Para Games in Hangzhou on Monday.Praveen clinched the gold medal for India with an impressive jump of 2.02 meters, securing the top position. Meanwhile, Unni demonstrated his skill by earning a well-deserved bronze medal for India in the men's high jump T64 final, leaping to a height of 1.95 meters.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) These victories have significantly contributed to India's overall success at the event, with a total of 17 medals, including six gold, six silver, and five bronze medals.India's dominance extends to athletics, where they have secured 11 of these medals, including five gold, three silver, and three bronze medals.India's performance at the Para Asian Games has been exceptional, with the country's best-ever performance being the 72 medals achieved in the 2018 edition held in Indonesia.The fourth Asian Para Games will continue until October 28, showcasing the incredible achievements and talents of para-athletes from across the region.

articles.title: India clinch 17 medals, including six gold, to begin Para Asian Games campaign in style
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Leading the way was star shooter Avani Lekhara, who clinched gold in the women's R2 10m air rifle standing SH1 category with a games record score of 2
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India had a remarkable start to the Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, securing a total of 17 medals on the opening day. This impressive haul included six gold, six silver, and five bronze medals. Leading the way was star shooter Avani Lekhara, who clinched gold in the women's R2 10m air rifle standing SH1 category with a games record score of 249.6.The day's events were dominated by track and field, contributing 11 of the 17 medals, including five gold. — AvaniLekhara (@AvaniLekhara) The morning commenced with Indian athletes sweeping all three medals in the men's club throw F51 event, where Pranav Soorma took home the gold. Soorma, who overcame a spinal cord injury at a young age, shattered the Asian Para Games record with a throw of 30.01m.There were only four competitors in the event with Saudi Arabia's Radhi Ali Alharthi finishing last with a throw of 23.77m.The F51 club throw event is for athletes who have movement affected to a high degree in the trunk, legs and hands. All the competitors compete while seated and rely on their shoulders and arm to generate power.Despite India's strong performance, they currently hold the fourth spot in the medals tally, trailing hosts China, Iran, and Uzbekistan. The Asian Para Games showcase the incredible achievements of para-athletes, and the Indian contingent's success on the first day sets a promising tone for the remainder of the competition."This gold is very special for me because this is my first medal in the Asian Para Games. This Asian Para Games is part of my preparations for the 2024 Paralympics," Avani said after winning gold.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) The other Indian para shooter Mona Agarwal finished sixth in the standings.Rudransh Khandelwal added a medal in shooting by winning a silver in P4 mixed 50m pistol SH1 event.Born in Jaipur in November 2001, Avani met with a road accident in 2012 that made her wheelchair-bound ever since.Inspired by Olympic champion Abhinav Bindra, her shooting career took off in 2015, and she has never looked back.Avani burst into the limelight with her stupendous show at the 2020 Tokyo Paralympics where she became the first Indian woman to win a gold medal in the Summer Games. There, Avani also won a bronze medal in the 50m rifle 3 positions.Three Indians also finished 1-2-3 in the men's high jump T63 category but only gold and silver were awarded under Asian Paralympic Committee (APC) rules.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) The three Indians were the only competitors in the event and under APC's 'minus one rule', Shailesh Kumar won the gold with an Asian Para Games record jump of 1.82m while Mariyappan Thangavelu (1.80m) took the silver.Govindbhai Ramsingbhai Padhiyar (1.78m) cannot win a bronze under APC rules.At least four athletes need to be in the fray to award all the three medals."In exceptional case where only three or fewer athletes compete, medal will be awarded following the 'minus-one rule'. For example, if an event is finalised by 2 athletes/teams only, only gold medal will be allocated," according to the APC rule book.The 23-year-old Kumar had won a silver in the World Para Athletics Championships earlier this year while Thangavelu was fourth. Both have qualified for next year's Paris Paralympics.Thangavelu had won a gold medal in high jump T42 category in 2016 Rio Paralympics and silver in T63 in Tokyo Paralympics.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) In T63 classification, athletes with a single leg above the knee amputation compete with a prosthesis.Nishad Kumar won India's third gold of the day in men's high jump T47 class as he cleared a height of 2.02m while compatriot Ram Pal took the bronze with an effort of 1.94m.The T47 classification is meant for athletes with a below elbow or wrist amputation or impairment.Nishad, a farmer's son in Amb town in Himachal Pradesh's Una district, got his right hand severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm when he was an eight-year-old.Ankur Dhama and Praveen Kumar clinched a gold each in men's 5000m T11 and high jump T64 events to complete the Indian medal rush.Ankur clocked 16:37.29 to win the race competed by runners with a near-total visual impairment.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Praveen cleared a games record height of 2.02m to win gold in the event meant for athletes with a leg amputation, who compete with prosthetics in a standing position. Another Indian, Renu Unni took the high jump T64 bronze.Monu Ghangas won the bronze medal in men's shot put F11 event with an effort of 12.33m.In women's canoe VL2 event, Prachi Yadav won a silver with a time of 1:03.147.In judo, Kapil Parmar picked up a silver in men's 60kg J1 event while Kokila won a bronze on women's 48kg J2 class.In taekwondo, Aruna picked up a bronze medal in women's 47kg K44 event.In para sports, athletes are classified according to the degree of activity limitation resulting from the impairment. Classification determines which athletes are eligible to compete in a particular event. This is done to ensure fair competition.(With PTI inputs)

articles.title: India bag 17 medals, including 3 gold on Day 2 of Hangzhou Asian Para Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India secured a total of 17 medals, which included three golds, bringing their overall count to 34 medals in the first two days of competition. The In
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prachi Yadav achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first Indian to win a gold medal in para canoe at the Asian Para Games in Hangzhou on Tuesday.India secured a total of 17 medals, which included three golds, bringing their overall count to 34 medals in the first two days of competition. The Indian contingent had previously earned 17 medals, including six golds, on Monday.India ended Day 2 placed fifth in the standings, one spot down from Monday, with nine gold, 12 silver and 13 bronze, behind China (165: 66 gold, 53 silver, 46 bronze), Iran (47), Japan (45) and Uzbekistan (38).Sharath Shankarappa Makanahalli won the men's T13 5000m event and his gold was initially counted and included in India's medal tally.But the number of India's gold medals was reduced to nine as there were only two competitors in the event.Under the Asian Paralympics Committee rulebook, it is up to the technical delegate to award medals in cases where there are less than three competitors.Prachi, who had secured a silver in the canoe VL2 category on Monday, added to her medal tally with a gold in the KL2 event.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Other athletes who won gold medals on Tuesday included Deepthi Jeevanji in women's T20 400m and Neeraj Yadav in men's F54/55/56 discus throw.Prachi, a 28-year-old athlete who is paralysed from the waist down, completed the 500m distance in 54.962 seconds to secure the gold in the KL2 event, a category for athletes who use their arms and have partial trunk and leg function to propel themselves. She hails from Gwalior.Prime Minister Narendra Modi appreciated the medal-winning efforts of the Indian athletes in a series of tweets."Congratulations to @ItzPrachi on winning the prestigious Gold Medal win in the Para Canoe Women's KL2 event. This was such an exceptional performance, which has made India proud. Best wishes for the endeavours ahead," Modi wrote on X, acknowledging the stupendous effort of Prachi.— narendramodi (@narendramodi) In the women's T20 category 400m race, Deepthi set a new Games and Asian record with her gold-winning time of 56.69 seconds. This category is designed for athletes with intellectual impairments.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) In the men's F54/55/56 discus throw event, Indian athletes swept all three medals. Neeraj Yadav clinched the gold with a Games and Asian record distance of 38.56m, while Yogesh Kathuniya (42.13m) and Muthuraja (35.06m) took home the silver and bronze, respectively.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Indian athletes also secured several silver and bronze medals on the day, showcasing their prowess in various events.In para shooting, Rudransh Khandelwal and Manish Narwal earned a silver and bronze, respectively, in the P1 men's 10m air pistol SH1 event, while Rubina Francis secured a bronze in the P2 women's 10m air pistol SH1 category.Bronze medalists on the day included Manish Kaurav (men's KL3 canoe), Ashok (men's 65kg powerlifting), Gajendra Singh (men's VL2 canoe), and Ekta Bhayan (women's F32/51 club throw).On the first day of competition, India had an outstanding performance, winning a total of 17 medals, including six gold medals, with star shooter Avani Lekhara leading the way.Apart from Avani (women's R2 10m air rifle standing SH1), the other gold medalists on Monday were Pranav Soorma (men's F51 club throw), Shailesh Kumar (men's T63 high jump), Nishad Kumar (men's T47 high jump), Ankur Dhama (men's T11 5000m), and Praveen Kumar (men's T64 high jump).India is represented by 313 athletes at the Hangzhou Para Asian Games, the largest contingent in any edition, with a target of winning 100 medals. The country is participating in 17 out of the 22 sports and has introduced athletes for the first time in rowing, canoeing, lawn bowls, taekwondo, and blind football.(With PTI inputs)

articles.title: Asian Para Games: India script history, achieve historic medal haul with 73 medals
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India's para-athletes have won their 16th gold medal at the Asian Para Games, and also surpassed their previous best medal tally of 72 medals from 201
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's para-athletes have made history by securing their highest-ever gold medal tally at the Asian Para Games, with the 16th gold medal won. India's outstanding performance has surpassed its previous best medal count of 72 at the 2018 Asian Para Games.Asian Para Games Day 4The historic 73rd medal in the ongoing Games in Hangzhou came from Nithya Sre, who clinched a remarkable bronze medal in the Women's Singles SH6 event. This achievement marks a historic moment for the Indian contingent, surpassing its previous best performance.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Notably, Indian shooter Sidhartha Babu played a pivotal role in this feat, securing a gold medal with a scintillating performance. Sidhartha achieved gold in the R6 Mixed 50m Rifles Prone SH-1 event, setting a new Asian Para Games Record with an impressive score of 247.7. This achievement also earned India a quota for the Paris 2024 Paralympics. Avani Lekhara participated in the same event and secured an 8th place finish in the finals.In Women's Shot Put-F34, Bhagyashri Madhavrao Jhadav claimed the silver medal with a remarkable throw of 7.54 metres, showcasing her incredible sporting prowess. In the Archery Men's Doubles - W1 Open event, Archer Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari and Naveen Dalal clinched a bronze medal with a remarkable score of 125-120.The flurry of medals continued on Day 4, with Sukant Kadam securing a bronze in Men's Badminton Singles SL-4 with an outstanding performance.— narendramodi (@narendramodi) India also shined in athletics on Day 4, securing a double podium finish in Men's Shot Put-F46. Sachin Khilari struck gold and set a Games Record with an impressive throw of 16.03 metres, while Rohit Hooda achieved a bronze medal with a personal best throw of 14.56 metres.In the Men's 100m T-37 event, Shreyansh Trivedi secured an impressive bronze with a remarkable time of 12.24 seconds.Para Athlete Narayan Thakur captured the bronze in the Men's 100m T-35 with a time of 14.37 seconds, marking his second medal at the Asian Para Games. (With inputs from ANI)

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Pramod Bhagat's clinches gold in badminton, Sheetal Devi wins a gold medal in archery
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Indian para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat won a gold medal in the men's singles SL 3 event at the 4th Asian Para Games, defeating his compatriot Nite
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-badminton player Pramod Bhagat showcased his excellence at the 4th Asian Para Games by clinching a gold medal in the badminton men's singles SL 3 event. In an all-Indian final, Pramod Bhagat triumphed over his compatriot Nitesh Kumar with a closely contested scoreline of 2-1, contributing to India's growing medal tally in the competition.The final was a highly competitive and thrilling encounter. Pramod Bhagat set the tone with a hard-fought victory in the first set, securing it 22-20 to take an early lead in the match. However, Nitesh Kumar mounted a comeback in the second set, leveling the game with a 21-18 scoreline. With his experience and skill, Pramod Bhagat sealed the deal by winning the deciding set 21-19, ultimately emerging victorious in the final with a 2-1 victory.— ParalympicIndia (@ParalympicIndia) In a different event, Indian para-badminton player Krishna Nagar, competing in the men's singles SH6 final, had to settle for a silver medal. He faced tough competition from Hong Kong's Man Kai Chu. While Krishna Nagar lost the first set, he made a remarkable comeback in the second, winning it 21-8. However, in the third and deciding set, Man Kai Chu showcased his dominance, securing a comfortable 21-11 victory.— ParalympicIndia (@ParalympicIndia) Earlier in the day, Indian archer Sheetal Devi started the day on a high note, winning a gold medal in the women's compound open event. Sheetal Devi displayed remarkable skill in archery as she triumphed over Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in a closely fought contest. Alim Nur had a one-point lead after the first three sets, but Sheetal Devi produced two consecutive perfect scores in the final two sets, securing the game with an overall score of 144-142.These achievements in para-badminton and archery are a testament to the skill and determination of Indian para-athletes, who continue to shine on the international stage, making their nation proud with their exceptional performances at the 4th Asian Para Games.(With ANI inputs)

articles.title: Indian para athletes create history with a record-breaking 111 medals at Hangzhou Asian Para Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Indian para athletes achieved a record 111 medals at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games, the most for the country in any major international multi-sport ev
articles.body: NEW DELHI: On Saturday, Indian para athletes made history by finishing their Hangzhou Asian Para Games campaign with a record 111 medals, the most for the country in any major international multi-sport event.The Indian para athletes won four more medals than the able-bodied athletes, with 29 gold, 31 silver, and 51 bronze in the Hangzhou Asian Games, which took place from September 23 to October 8.India finished fifth in the medal count, trailing China (521 medals: 214 gold, 167 silver, 140 bronze), Iran (44 gold, 46 silver, 41 bronze), Japan (42, 49, 59), and Korea (30, 33, 40).The first Para Asian Games were held in Guangzhou, China, in 2010, with India finishing 15th with 14 medals, including one gold.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) India finished 15th and eighth in the 2014 and 2018 tournaments, respectively.The only time India had won 100 medals in a major international multi-sport event (Olympics, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games) was at the 2010 Delhi Commonwealth Games."We have made history, our para athletes have made the country proud. We will win more medals in the Paris Paralympics than in Tokyo," Paralympic Committee of India president Deepa Malik told PTI."However, it is not a surprise for us. We expected between 110 to 115 medals and we ended at 111, the auspicious number (Angel Number)," she added.Asian Para Games Day 6On Thursday, India surpassed the previous best Asian Para Games tally of 72 medals (15 gold, 24 silver, 33 bronze) set in 2018.India earned 39 more medals than in 2018, with athletics accounting for 55 (18 gold, 17 silver, and 20) of India's total of 111.With 21, including four gold medals, Indian shuttlers came in second. Chess and archery each received eight medals, while shooting received six.On the final day, India collected 12 medals, including four gold. Chess won seven medals, athletics won four, and rowing won one.Neeraj Yadav began the day with a gold medal in men's javelin throw F55, setting a Games record of 33.69m. In the same event, compatriot Tek Chand won bronze with a personal best of 30.36m.Dilip Mahadu Gaviot won the men's 400m T47 competition in 49.48 seconds, adding another gold medal to his collection.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Pooja then won the final athletics medal, a bronze medal in the women's 1500m T20 race in 5:38.81s.Chess players saved the best for last with a seven-medal assault on the last day, including two gold medals.Satish Inani Darpan won gold in the men's individual rapid VI-B1 event, while Pradhan Kumar Soundarya and Ashwinbhai Kanchanbhai Makwana took silver and bronze, respectively. The trio also won the team gold medal.Kishan Gangoli finished third in the men's individual rapid VI-B2/B3 event. In the same event, Gangoli, Somendra, and Aryan Balchandra Joshi won bronze as a team.In the women's fast VI-B1 team event, Vruthi Saganlal Jain, Himanshi Bhaveshkumar Rathi, and Sanskruti Vikas More won bronze.On Saturday, Anita and Konganapalle Narayana earned a silver medal in the PR3 mixed double sculls event, giving India its lone medal in rowing.India sent 313 competitors to the Hangzhou Para Asian Games, the most in any edition, including 51 Tokyo Paralympians.India competed in 17 of the 22 sports, including rowing, canoeing, lawn bowl, taekwondo, and blind football for the first time.The Hangzhou Asian Para Games include nearly 4,000 participants from 43 countries participating in 566 gold-medal events across 22 sports.The Hangzhou Asian Para Games were initially slated for October 9-15, 2022, but were pushed back a year because of the COVID-19 epidemic.(With inputs from PTI)

articles.title: Army jawan's wife wins two silver medals at Para Asian Games
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: "She is born a fighter. I cannot express my happiness in words. Really proud of her achievement," said Naik Gajendra Singh, who is coach-cum-husband o
articles.body: LUCKNOW: "She is born a fighter. I cannot express my happiness in words. Really proud of her achievement," said Naik Gajendra Singh, who is coach-cum-husband of athlete Simran Sharma, after she won back-to-back silver medals in 100m and 200m dash at Para Asian Games in Hangzhou, China.Born with impaired vision condition which makes it difficult for her to see beyond seven to 10 meters, the 24-year-old athlete clocked 12.68 seconds for 100m on October 24 and 26.12 seconds for 200m on October 26 in final heat, to win medals.Back in 2021, she became the first Indian woman para-athlete to qualify for the 100-metre track event in Tokyo Paralympics. However, she failed to fetch a medal. Earlier in the month of July this year, two days before her race at Paris World Para Athletics Championships, Simran sustained severe thigh muscle injury and doctor had advised her to rest for a year for complete recovery, however she and her coach worked together on her injury and prepared themselves for Asian games."After Tokyo Paralympics setback, Simran’s injury just two days before the race at Paris World Para Athletics Championships had really shattered us. But she was determined not to give up. A week before the Asian games, Simran was highly confident with her physic and we both stayed focused for the race, "said 30-year-old Gajendra, who is currently posted in New Delhi’s 227 company of Army Service Corps.The couple are set to return to India on October 31, where they are expected to be felicitated by Army Chief Manoj Pande as well as by Gajendra’s unit separately."My unit gave me free hand to help my wife in her endeavor. We have received a congratulatory message after the win," added Gajendra who tied knot with Simran in 2017. Meanwhile speaking to TOI, Simran said, "I was born as a preterm infant and was kept for seven months in an incubator. Doctors had given up hope and were not sure of my survival. But 24 years later, I had proved my mettle. All this was possible because of my husband's support. The sports authority of India and others who too played a vital role in grooming me for international level races."After their return to India, the couple will start preparing for the World Championships which is going to be held in Japan in 2024. Couple hails from Modi Nagar of Ghaziabad district, Uttar Pradesh.

articles.title: Lebron ya no es el rey
articles.standfirst: 1XBET sitúa a Oklahoma City Thunder y San Antonio Spurs como grandes favoritos justo antes del arranque de la temporada
articles.summary: 1XBET sitúa a Oklahoma City Thunder y San Antonio Spurs como grandes favoritos justo antes del arranque de la temporada
articles.body: La temporada 2026/27 de la NBA está a punto de comenzar, y llega precedida de uno de los veranos más movidos que se recuerdan. Los New York Knicks levantaron su primer anillo en 53 años tras derrotar a los San Antonio Spurs en las Finales, poniendo fin a una racha de ocho campeones distintos en ocho años consecutivos. Pero apenas se secó el confeti de la celebración, el mercado de fichajes volvió a sacudir la liga con un movimiento sísmico. LeBron James, a sus 42 años, decidió unirse a los Philadelphia 76ers, formando un cuarteto de lujo junto a Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey y Jaylen Brown, este último procedente de los Boston Celtics. Pese a todos estos movimientos sobre la mesa, las casas de apuestas, como 1XBET, sitúan al Oklahoma City Thunder como principal favorito para levantar el título, a cuota 3.6. El equipo de Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, bicampeón consecutivo del premio MVP, llega con la espina clavada de haber caído en el séptimo partido de la final de la Conferencia Oeste ante los propios Spurs la pasada primavera, y con el objetivo de recuperar el trono que ostentó en 2025. Muy cerca aparece San Antonio, a cuota 3.7, un equipo que gira en torno a Victor Wembanyama, flamante Mejor Defensor del Año de forma unánime y que acaba de firmar una extensión de cinco años y 252 millones de dólares con la franquicia texana como muestra de compromiso a largo plazo. En tercer lugar aparecen los Philadelphia 76ers, a cuota 9.5 en las apuestas deportivas de 1XBET. Las expectativas en torno a Philly son enormes tras la llegada de Lebron, aunque persisten las dudas sobre si el conjunto de Nick Nurse tiene la profundidad y la salud necesarias para sostener un nivel competitivo a lo largo de las 82 jornadas de temporada regular, algo que muchos analistas consideran su verdadero techo antes de llegar a los playoffs. Por otro lado, resulta especialmente llamativo que los propios New York Knicks, vigentes campeones con Jalen Brunson como MVP de las Finales, aparezcan solo cuartos en las quinielas, a cuota 10. La explicación reside en lo extraordinariamente difícil que resulta revalidar el título en la NBA moderna. Ningún equipo lo ha logrado en los últimos ocho años Cierra el grupo de cabeza Boston, a cuota 15, un equipo que ha visto salir a una de sus piezas clave, Jaylen Brown, precisamente rumbo a Filadelfia, pero que conserva argumentos suficientes para seguir peleando en una Conferencia Este que se presenta más competitiva que nunca. Con Oklahoma City y San Antonio marcando el paso, unos Knicks decididos a repetir gesta histórica y unos 76ers reforzados hasta el extremo, la temporada 2026/27 promete continuar la era de paridad que vive la NBA en los últimos años.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Why we're in total panic-mode with Colston Loveland, Rashee Rice and more
articles.summary: It's time for Ray Garvin's latest Panic Meter coming off Week 2 of the 2026 fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Two weeks into the fantasy football season, we have officially reached the point where every bad box score starts to feel like a problem. But there is a difference between a player failing to produce and a player failing to earn opportunities. That is what I care about most when deciding whether it is actually time to panic.

Draft cost matters because expectations matter, but routes, targets, target share and the quality of those opportunities tells us a lot more about what is actually happening.

For this Panic Meter, the thresholds are simple: No Panic, Some Panic, Total Panic or Coping Corner. Not every slow start deserves the same level of concern.

Five targets. One catch. Three receiving yards. That's Loveland through two games.

For a player drafted inside the top-40 picks on Yahoo, there is no way to make that sound good.

There are at least a few signs that tell us this hasn't been a complete zero. Loveland has generated 12.27 expected PPR points compared to just 1.3 actual points and has already seen two end-zone targets. He also played 87% of Chicago's offensive snaps in Week 2.

So yes, he's on the field. Yes, he has left points out there. But even those expected points only come out to 6.13 per game. That's the part I keep coming back to. Positive regression only matters so much if the workload itself isn't strong enough.

You're clearly not dropping Loveland, but you absolutely need another playable tight end on your roster until this role improves. I need to see more routes and actual target earning, not just another game where he's on the field a ton — but barely involved.

If you only look at Rice's fantasy totals, you might wonder why he's even on this list. He has 22.2 PPR points through two games. He scored in Week 1. He went for 83 yards in Week 2.

Rice has turned those opportunities into 22.2 PPR points despite just 12.91 expected points. That production has covered up what has been a pretty underwhelming workload for a receiver drafted this high.

And Kansas City gave us plenty of passing volume in Week 2. The Chiefs had 51 dropbacks and threw for 382 yards. Travis Kelce had 11 targets, Kenneth Walker had 10, Xavier Worthy had seven and Rice had six.

That's where the concern comes from. This wasn't an offense that couldn't move the ball or couldn't create passing volume. There were targets available — Rice just wasn't commanding enough of them.

I'm not moving off the player just because of two games, but I am absolutely adjusting what I expect from him right now. Another touchdown doesn't solve this. I want to see Rice become a priority in this passing game again.

Pickens hasn't given fantasy managers much yet. Nine catches. 68 yards. No touchdowns. Just 15.8 PPR points through two weeks. But this is one where the process looks better than the results.

Pickens has already earned 14 targets and those opportunities have been worth 23.11 expected PPR points. He saw eight targets in Week 2 alone and caught six of them.

Dallas threw four touchdowns in that game. Pickens just didn't get one.

That's frustrating, but it's also why I don't want to overreact. I'm much more comfortable waiting on production when the player is still earning the football.

Through two games, Pickens owns roughly 23% of the Cowboys' targets in my data. That is enough involvement for me to stay patient, even if I'd still like to see stronger route participation and more explosive production.

I'm watching it, but I'm not worried enough to make a bad decision. If someone else sees the box scores and thinks Pickens has already failed, I'm interested in finding out how aggressively they're willing to move him.

My concern with Egbuka isn't really that Egbuka has been bad. He hasn't.

Through two games, he has 11 targets, eight catches, 79 yards and a touchdown. His 21.6 actual PPR points are basically right in line with his 23.01 expected points.

The problem is what has been happening around him.

Baker Mayfield has been disappointing to start the season and this Zac Robinson offense has looked bad. That's a pretty important piece of this conversation because there is only so much Egbuka can do if the passing game never finds any rhythm.

Week 2 is the perfect example. Egbuka finished with five targets and just 16 receiving yards. The touchdown saved his fantasy day.

That works for one week. I don't want to depend on it every week. So I'm at Some Panic with Egbuka.

The player still looks fine to me. The role hasn't disappeared. But I need Baker to play better and I need this passing offense to give Egbuka more chances to produce without requiring a touchdown to get there.

Jamo's two-game totals are a little misleading. He has 13 targets, six catches and 78 yards. He has scored 13.8 PPR points against 25.34 expected points.

That sounds like an obvious case of a guy who's just been unlucky.

Week 1? Maybe. He generated 19.53 expected PPR points in that game and only scored 8.5. That's the kind of gap where you can talk yourself into patience.

Week 2 is what changed this for me. Detroit dropped back 44 times. Jared Goff threw four touchdowns. Williams played 97% of the snaps and ran 40 routes.

You can give me all the routes and snaps in the world, but at some point the football has to find you. When an offense throws that much and scores that much and you're still sitting at just four targets, I have to pay attention.

And Detroit's defense has looked bad enough that this offense should continue finding itself in games where it has to keep scoring. That's a positive environment for pass catchers, but it also makes the lack of targets harder to ignore.

I'm not cutting Jamo, but I am absolutely adjusting expectations. If Detroit keeps getting pushed into scoring mode and Williams is still running this many routes without commanding the football, then this stops being a bad-luck conversation and starts becoming a role conversation.

articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 3: Latest news, updates for Caleb Williams, Jaxson Dart, more with fantasy football analysis
articles.summary: We're going over the Week 3 NFL injury report to help with your fantasy football lineup decisions.
articles.body:
The NFL injury report is starting to get crowded as we head into Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season. Among those injured in Week 2 was Bears QB Caleb Williams, who suffered what appeared to be a pretty bad lower-body injury at the time . Turns out, Williams sustained a hamstring injury that has him week-to-week going into a matchup vs. the Eagles on Monday Night Football.

On top of that, the Commanders could be without QB Jayden Daniels long-term after he suffered another elbow injury — something he dealt with last season — in the team's loss to the Cowboys in Week 2. And then on MNF, the Giants lost starter Jaxson Dart to a knee injury that could hold him out. It's tough out there in the QB fantasy streets.

We'll be monitoring their statuses moving forward, as well as a handful of notable players for fantasy football in Week 3.

Jaxson Dart, NYG (knee) — Could miss rest of season

Kyler Murray , MIN (concussion) — Will Play

Michael Penix Jr., ATL (knee) — Will Start Week 3

Dart : The Giants got the worst news possible later on Monday as the injury for Dart is more serious than initially thought. He's going to miss an extended period of time, which could be the entire 2026 season, per ESPN . Jameis Winston struggled in relief on Monday, completing just 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and one INT. As a result, the Giants only mustered 183 total yards (some of those were before Dart got hurt). This is a major downgrade for Giants' skill position players, namely Malik Nabers , Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely . Though, New York does have a solid matchup in Week 3 vs. the Titans at home. It's tough to see this offense staying afloat with Winston at the helm all season.

Bagent : Things just got a bit worse for the Bears and Ben Johnson. Bagent has been placed into the NFL's concussion protocol and now his status for Week 3 vs. the Eagles on MNF is up in the air. He'll have the extra day to clear, but it's usually pretty tough to do so in this little amount of time. If Bagent can't start, Chicago will turn to Case Keenum right now. It's unclear who would be promoted to serve as his backup or if the Bears would opt to bring someone else in to possibly start. This is just another QB injury we'll need to monitor closely this week.

Penix : The Falcons cleared Penix for Week 3's matchup vs. the Packers on Thursday Night Football. He will be welcome addition to the offense, which has struggled mightily in two games with Cooper Rush/Jack Strand under center. With Penix in the lineup, it should be a huge boost for pass-catchers Drake London and Kyle Pitts Sr., as well as star RB Bijan Robinson .

Williams : As was stated above, Williams is week-to-week with the hamstring issue, which is a great sign that he avoided major injury. The Bears will likely proceed with Tyson Bagent at QB in Week 3 vs. the Eagles, assuming Williams can't play. Head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Williams will "likely miss some time." Bagent is a serviceable backup who has shown flashes of decent play in the past. But he's a very clear downgrade from Williams. Chicago pass-catchers Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland had already been underperforming through two weeks. They'll carry a significant amount of risk in Week 3 should Williams sit. We could see Johnson lean more heavily on RBs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai in the short-term.

Daniels : The Commanders' signal-caller is dealing with a dislocated left elbow but doesn't have a fracture, which is a positive. Still, it's the same injury he suffered last season in Week 9. We don't have a timeline on a return for Daniels, but backup Marcus Mariota should start in Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. For this week, with such a difficult matchup, it may be wise to fade Washington entirely. Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs would be risky flex options, even in PPR formats. In easier matchups, Mariota has shown the ability to buoy the offense, and he did find Diggs for a TD in Week 2 after Daniels left.

Murray : Kyler has cleared concussion protocol and will start for the Vikings in Week 3 vs. the Bucs . It's difficult to gather anything from Week 2's 9-3 win over the Bears given the weather. We also only saw Murray for barely a series before he exited in Week 1 vs. the Packers. We'll have to see how he fares before making any type of assessment. For now, Murray is more of a QB2 until we know more. Luckily, there have been plenty of QBs who have emerged as strong fantasy options you can likely scoop up off the waiver wire .

Broncos backfield : Harvey was inactive for the Broncos' win over the Jaguars in Week 2. Dobbins exited the game early, which paved the way for rookie Jonah Coleman to have a larger role. He's going to be a trendy waiver wire claim going into Week 3. Justin Boone has more on Coleman and how to approach him off the wire here .

Barkley : We're awaiting more information on Barkley's stinger, which caused him to miss a big chunk of the comeback win over the Titans on Sunday. As a result, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches for 38 yards and a score. Should Barkley miss any time, Bigsby would become the lead back with Will Shipley also in the mix. Bigsby is another name Boone mentions as a top waiver consideration for Week 3.

Price : You're going to sense a trend here. Price left in the fourth quarter of the Seahawks' easy win over the Cardinals in Week 2. This injury doesn't appear to be serious, so there's a chance Price is good to go for Week 3 vs. the Commanders. It's worth noting Emanuel Wilson was heavily involved in Week 2, rushing 21 times for 92 yards. George Holani also got five touches. Price did lose a fumble in the game but should remain the focal point of the rushing attack when healthy. If you have Price, it's worth adding Wilson just in case. If Price is sidelined, Wilson would get a solid boost into RB2/3 territory.

Nacua : The Rams sat Nacua on MNF in Week 2 vs. the Giants. It led to a massive performance from Davante Adams , who hauled in eight of 10 targets for 195 yards and two TDs. He finished as the WR2 in fantasy, trailing only Jaxon Smith-Njigba and his hat trick from Sunday. HC Sean McVay is hopeful Nacua can suit up in Week 3 vs. the Broncos. If Nacua remains out, Adams is a borderline WR1, though he draws a tough matchup vs. Pat Surtain II. Terrance Ferguson would also be more involved after his solid 6-54-1 line vs. New York.

Nabers : The wide receiver exited MNF vs. the Rams after his shoulder got dislocated . He popped it back in and was able to return to the game, stating that he's "OK" post-game. Nabers is schedule to undergo X-rays, so we'll wait and see what the results show. For now, monintor Nabers' status during practice but know that with Dart sidelined, his fantasy value takes a pretty big hit. Tennessee presents a good matchup in Week 3, but Nabers should be downgraded to a risky WR2/3 in PPR formats.

Collins : The Texans were without Collins for their tough loss to the Bengals in Week 2. The offense struggled, clearly missing its top wideout and target for C.J. Stroud . TE Dalton Schultz was the biggest beneficiary, finishing as the TE2 overall in fantasy after Sunday, catching 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards. Houston has a big game vs. the Colts in Week 3 and the expectation is for Collins to remain out . Indy has allowed 74 points through two games this season, so there's a good chance the Texans can get something going, which could bode well for Xavier Hutchinson , Kayshon Boutte and Jaylin Noel .

Moore : The Bills wideout is considered day-to-day with an AC joint sprain. He's had extra time to get right after suffering the injury on TNF vs. the Lions in Week 2. If Moore is active, he's a solid WR2/3 in a good matchup vs. the Chargers. If Moore is out, Keon Coleman , Khalil Shakir and Josh Palmer should get the majority of the snaps at WR. Dalton Kincaid has been Josh Allen 's favorite target so far this season and that should continue with or without Moore in Week 3.

Pierce : The Colts wide receiver was forced to exit TNF vs. the Chiefs after aggravating the same heel/ankle injury that kept him sidelined during training camp . There's no clear timeline for Pierce's return. If Pierce misses time, it's a bump up for Josh Downs and Tyler Warren . Laquan Treadwell shockingly saw 74% of the snaps in the loss to the Chiefs, which was more than veteran Keenan Allen , who only caught one of his five targets for five yards.

Goedert : The Eagles' pass-catcher is expected to miss a few weeks after spraining his MCL in Week 2 vs. the Titans, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. After finishing as a TE1 last season, Goedert got off to a hot start with 4-77-2 in Week 1 to finish as the TE2 overall. He had just one catch for four yards before leaving on Sunday. Philly is now down its top-two TEs in Goedert and rookie Eli Stowers , who is on injured reserve with a hamstring issue. Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins split the snaps at TE vs. Tennessee, and Mundt was targetted three times. He isn't really a viable streaming option at TE if you have Goedert, so look to Boone's waiver wire guide for Week 3 for advice . The Eagles offense is getting pretty banged up, which isn't great. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks should continue to lead the passing game, though don't sleep on Darius Cooper .

Bowers : Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters after the team's win in Week 2 that Bowers is "very close" to returning. That could mean we see him suit up in Week 3 vs. the Saints, though with Las Vegas 2-0 to start the season, the team could be cautious with the top pass-catcher. With Bowers out again, it was Michael Mayer who got the majority of the TE snaps at 84%. Cody White isn't technically a tight end but he caught two TDs that likely would have been layups for Bowers had he been healthy. Mayer will continue to be a decent streaming option at TE in Week 3 if Bowers sits again. There should be plenty of points in the Saints-Raiders matchup.

articles.title: Devin Booker's Possible Regression Isn’t Concern for Phoenix Suns
articles.summary: Skeptics question Devin Booker’s superstar trajectory as Phoenix faces looming roster uncertainties, testing whether the franchise cornerstone can overcome a...
articles.body:
The 2026-27 season is right around the corner for the Phoenix Suns .

Phoenix is just one month away from tipping the regular season off with a road game against the Portland Trail Blazers .

While internal expectations and hopes from the fans are quite lofty, the outside world doesn't seem to be showing the team quite the same amount of love.

Part of this ensemble is Kevin O'Connor of Yahoo Sports, who ranks the Suns as the 20th best team in the NBA heading into training camp.

The 15-20 range seems to be a customary placing for Phoenix at the moment, but O'Connor's concern is perhaps the most jarring part of the evaluation of the Suns.

"Can Booker get back to superstar form?"

There's little doubt that franchise star Devin Booker has experienced a slight downtick in scoring volume and efficiency as of late.

Even if Booker isn't a top-five level scorer any longer - or hasn't reached the heights that the 2023 postseason run demonstrated he can reach - he is still one of the best players in the league.

The 6'5" shooting guard is still evolving as a playmaker, is still one of the craftiest scorers in the entire league, and presents gravity that creates advantages for rising stars such as Collin Gillespie .

Is Booker a perfect player? Absolutely not. However, it feels trivial to question his ability to lead a team in 2026, especially after the five-time All-Star led Phoenix to a playoff appearance in a season that multiple co-stars missed extensive time due to injury. The question shouldn't be framed around Booker's decline, it should be as to whether the Kentucky product has an ability to become a ceiling raiser yet again.

Phoenix has several other concerns that are much more pressing than Booker. Among these concerns are the uncertain center rotation with the absence of Mark Williams . There is also the question if the Suns will be able to capture the exceptional three-point shooting magic they did in 2025-26. Beyond this, the fit of incoming forward Miles Bridges and guard Luke Kennard is one that will test head coach Jordan Ott.

Even if one wants to state that Booker is regressing, this is far from the most substantial concern at the moment for the Suns' organization. This will become apparent very early in the season for those that are skeptical about this conversation.

The Hornets later included Hawkins in a trade package to the Seattle SuperSonics for Kendall Gill. After four seasons with Seattle and one with the Chicago Bulls , Hawkins signed a one-year deal with the Hornets and finished his career in Charlotte. In 59 games for the Hornets the second time around, Hawkins averaged 3.1 points, 1.4 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 0.6 steals.

The former No. 6 overall pick finished his 13-year NBA career with one All-Star appearance, a sportsmanship award and averages of 14.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 1.7 steals.

articles.title: Mike Macdonald's comments about Sean Payton weren't intended for public consumption
articles.summary: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald launched his career as a head coach with a win over Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos . The game from September 2024 moved back to the front burner on Tuesday, thanks to footage from Macdonald's recent interview with Graham Bensinger.

The excerpt , which wasn't released when the first clips and quotes began to be circulated, relates to a squabble that emerged regarding the use by the Seahawks of fan-generated video from Broncos training-camp practices. It got ugly , as Macdonald told the story to Bensinger.

It could get ugly between the Seahawks and Bensinger's camp. As we understand it, the conversation was not intended by Macdonald for public consumption. The Seahawks, we're told, didn't even know that portion of the "more off than on" the record discussion had been recorded until Tuesday morning.

The situation is another reminder that everything is potentially on the record, absent a clear agreement between the parties that it's not. And while Bensinger's people didn't breach any journalistic rules by using it, the fact that it was posted could make future subjects more leery about agreeing to be interviewed.

On or off the record, others are befuddled by Macdonald's decision to air gripes from two years ago. And there's a question as to whether the various things Macdonald said to Bensinger (regarding Payton and others) are the product of arrogance or naiveté.

"What's the point?" said one source connected to neither the Seahawks nor the Broncos. "It was reckless."

The Broncos declined comment on the situation. Undoubtedly, Payton will be asked about it when he conducts his usual Wednesday press conference.

Either way, the kerfuffle adds a little extra sizzle to a spicy Week 6 Thursday night game between the two teams.

articles.title: Things will only go from bad to worse for Chargers against red-hot Josh Allen, Bills
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are embarrassing themselves in front of the entire football community. There really isn’t a nicer way to put it after two weeks. The...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are embarrassing themselves in front of the entire football community.

There really isn't a nicer way to put it after two weeks. The Chargers entered the season with legitimate Super Bowl expectations after an aggressive offseason, yet they are 0-2 after consecutive 26-14 losses to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders . Neither game looked like an unfortunate loss, either. Los Angeles has looked unprepared, undisciplined, and completely lost for extended stretches.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Chargers now travel to Buffalo to face Josh Allen and a Bills team that looks absolutely terrifying. Buffalo has scored 77 points through two games, including 41 against Detroit on Thursday night, and Allen already looks like he's building another MVP-caliber season.

That's the last opponent Los Angeles needs right now.

Mike McDaniel 's offense has been a mess through two games. The offensive line has struggled to consistently protect Justin Herbert , receivers aren't creating enough separation, and Herbert has responded by forcing throws he normally wouldn't make. He deserves some of the blame, too. Herbert hasn't consistently recognized pressure quickly enough and threw two interceptions against Las Vegas while completing only 15 of 27 passes.

But the Chargers aren't exactly helping their franchise quarterback. The penalties, turnovers, protection breakdowns and general confusion make it look like an offense still trying to figure out what it wants to be. Now David Njoku and Charlie Kolar are both headed to injured reserve , removing two tight ends from an offense that desperately needs reliable options.

That's before even getting to the defense.

Chargers' defense might be walking into a nightmare against Josh Allen

Chris O'Leary inherited a defense that Jesse Minter helped turn into one of the NFL's better units over the previous two seasons. Through two games, however, Los Angeles hasn't looked nearly as aggressive or disruptive.

The Chargers have frequently kept their secondary deep and asked their defensive front to create pressure without consistently bringing additional rushers. That can work when Khalil Mack , Tuli Tuipulotu , and Akheem Mesidor are taking over games. Outside of flashes, that hasn't happened enough yet, and Los Angeles hasn't consistently forced opposing quarterbacks into uncomfortable situations.

Trying that against Allen sounds like a disaster waiting to happen.

Allen just shredded Detroit for 248 passing yards and three touchdowns while adding 69 rushing yards and two more scores. Buffalo scored touchdowns on five of its first six possessions and built a 27-10 halftime advantage against a Lions team that entered the season with championship aspirations.

The Chargers are supposed to slow that down? This defense could get carved up like a pumpkin pie on Thanksgiving if they don't change something up quickly.

Los Angeles is also dealing with injuries defensively, including Derwin James playing through a finger issue . Asking an already struggling defense to contain Allen, James Cook , and Buffalo's collection of weapons without generating immediate pressure could turn Sunday's game ugly very quickly. Look for former Chargers receiver Josh Palmer to make a play or two.

Herbert might have to become Los Angeles' version of Allen just to keep the Chargers competitive. Buffalo's defense has allowed 31 points in each of its first two games, so opportunities should exist for McDaniel and Herbert to finally get the offense moving. The problem is that Buffalo's pass rush has already produced seven sacks, creating another brutal matchup for a Chargers offense struggling with protection.

This isn't necessarily a must-win game in September, but 0-3 would create a hole nobody expected Los Angeles to be digging out of this early.

The Chargers spent the offseason convincing everyone they were ready to contend with the AFC's best.

They're about to find out exactly how far away they really are.

articles.summary: The Arizona Diamondbacks began their final regular-season road trip of 2026 on Tuesday, Sept. 22, in Denver. Follow our live updates.
articles.body:
DENVER — The Diamondbacks came into their game on Tuesday, Sept. 22, against the Rockies at Coors Field in need of six wins, in their minds, over their final six games of the regular season to have a shot at a National League wild-card spot.

They entered the night four games behind the Philadelphia Phillies and five behind the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres .

"Focus on what we do well, focus on doing your job and not worrying about anything else," Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo said prior to the first of three games against Colorado . "Little things matter. Do little things and let them add up to a big moment.

"We know what we've got to do. We've got to go out and win every baseball game. I don't like thinking like that. I just want us to win today. I want us to play our finest game today and at the end of the day, we'll see where we're at."

Ketel Marte , who has a history of not playing an entire series when the Diamondbacks visit Colorado due to health reasons, was in the lineup as the designated hitter. Lovullo said he planned to have Marte play defense the last two games of the series.

"I don't want to ask anybody to go out there and empty their tank," Lovullo said. "We know what we've got to get to, and I'm going to ask guys to go and give me just a little bit extra."

See Arizona Diamondbacks' 3-game series vs New York Yankees in photos

Burnes to remain in rotation, Moreno's workload

The Diamondbacks, if they stick with how they've set up their pitching rotation, will turn to right-hander Corbin Burnes on Saturday, Sept. 26, at San Diego in what could still be a game to stay alive in the wild-card race.

"We'll probably just trust what he's given us and his own personal evaluation. He feels strong, he feels healthy," Lovullo said of Burnes, who spent 15 months trying to get back from elbow surgery and a subsequent injury.

Catcher Gabriel Moreno continues to play without much rest at all. Moreno is so vital to the Diamondbacks with his consistent hitting and defense that Lovullo continues to go to him.

"He's in that category where you can't win games without him," Lovullo said. "We've got to manage his workload. I caught him three days in a row before the off day (Monday). I haven't done that all year long. He's going to probably catch five of the last six games, depending on what the needs are.

"In the game that he doesn't catch, I'm probably going to DH him. But he's been so impactful for us."

Moreno said the key for him to have reached career highs in games played, at-bats, runs scored, hits, home runs and runs batted in is staying healthy this season. Tuesday was Moreno's 126th game of the season, out of 157.

"Just going to do my best in everything I can," Moreno said. "Running, hitting, catching, helping the team win."

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: New Delhi: She wasn't supposed to be in Aich-Nagoya. Not at the Asian Games. Not at her third successive continental event. And certainly not one win .
articles.body: New Delhi: She wasn't supposed to be in Aich-Nagoya. Not at the Asian Games. Not at her third successive continental event. And certainly not one win away from a place in the women's 60kg sanda final.Naorem Roshibina Devi had lost fairly in the selection trials for the Games, held in Srinagar in June. Her teammate Divyanshi Choudhary beat her in the semifinals and went on to win the trials, earning the original berth in India's wushu squad.Asian Games Full Coverage| Schedule| Medal TallyRoshibina had accepted her fate. The federation replaced her with Roshibina, reopening a door the Manipuri had thought was firmly shut.And she has made the most of it.On Tuesday, Roshibina defeated Macau's Chu Man Sin 5-0 in the women's 60kg sanda quarterfinal at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall to storm into the semifinals and assure herself of at least a bronze medal. A day earlier, she had beaten Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarters.Now she has a chance to go one step further — and change the colour of her medal.The 25-year-old has already changed colours once at the Asian Games. After her bronze in Jakarta, she ended India's 13-year wait for a wushu silver at Hangzhou, finishing second in the same 60kg sanda event.Now, another medal is assured, gold is her target.Her return to the squad, however, came amid a controversy. articles.title: Gary Bettman Gives Update on NHL Expansion, Talks Decision Timeline Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: NHL commissioner Gary Bettman told reporters on Tuesday that the league's board of governors is taking a "wait-and-see attitude" regarding the potential to add two more expansion franchises.
articles.body:
NHL commissioner Gary Bettman told reporters on Tuesday that the league's board of governors is taking a "wait-and-see attitude" regarding the potential to add two more expansion franchises.

"We continue to evaluate and receive expressions of interest, which I guess is a really good thing," he added.

The league reportedly has received interest from the Friedkin family regarding a potential expansion team in both Houston and Austin.

"I don't think we're putting time limits on things. We're working through the process. They're working through the process," Bettman said regarding the Friedkin family's evaluation regarding Houston or Austin. "Originally, we contemplated at least knowing where we are in December. I expect we will certainly know a lot more than we do now, come December, but I don't think there's any magic date by which something has to get done or not get done."

Other groups have expressed interest in potentially bringing teams to Atlanta and Phoenix, both former homes to NHL organizations.

"Expansion is a multibillion-dollar transaction, which has an impact on all the other clubs in the league," Bettman said. "If there's going to be expansion, three-quarters of the governors are going to have to be comfortable that this makes sense to them. And that's not something you do overnight."

The NHL last expanded in 2021, adding the Seattle Kraken to bring the league to 32 franchises. Prior to that, the Vegas Golden Knights were added in 2016.

articles.title: How a Nagoya baseball ground was transformed into an Asian Games cricket venue
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Nagoya: On the sidelines of the cricket facility at Korogi Athletic Park, a few Sri Lankan men sat watching the India-Sri Lanka women’s final. Not far.
articles.body: Nagoya: On the sidelines of the cricket facility at Korogi Athletic Park, a few Sri Lankan men sat watching the India-Sri Lanka women’s final. Not far away, an Australian kept a close eye on the proceedings.They were not casual spectators. They were among the men who helped turn a baseball ground in a public park on the outskirts of Nagoya into a cricket venue capable of hosting the best teams in Asia.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThe journey began in late September last year, when the decision was taken to include cricket in this edition of the Asian Games. A little over 300 million yen was earmarked to create the infrastructure, including temporary stands with a capacity of 2,500 spectators.Korogi was chosen because of the size of the facility. The Japan Cricket Association (JCA) also had a head start, having signed an MoU with Sri Lanka Cricket in March 2024, paving the way for Sri Lankan curators to be brought in.At the centre of the operation was Jarrad Shearer, an Australian who has lived in Japan for the past 30 years.“When it was decided that cricket would be part of the Asian Games, Alex Miyaji, the CEO of the JCA, approached me for a role because I had played some cricket back home in Perth and knew Japanese,” Shearer, a sports manager in the planning section of the organising committee, told TOI.The transformation was no small job. The existing facility consisted of three baseball diamonds, with lines of trees demarcating the playing areas. The first task was to clear the trees and level the ground.“We did the pitch and the outfield at the same time. While we were digging a hole to build the pitch, we were laying the outfield. So we created one hybrid wicket and four turf wickets,” said Shearer, who is also a Japanese translator by profession.Gamini de Silva, former curator of Bangladesh’s Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium, and Asitha Wijesinghe, curator of Sri Lanka’s Pallekele International Stadium, came on board. They were joined by a few Sri Lankan-origin residents of Japan who had experience as groundsmen.“While the four groundsmen are from here, Gamini and Asitha took turns to be here to oversee the preparations,” Shearer said.Pitch construction, however, presented one of the biggest challenges.“The pitch construction was interesting because we had a Japanese company doing it and they didn’t know anything about turf wickets. So our planning and instructions had to be spot on,” he said.The pitches were built using layers of gravel, washed riverbed soil and 15cm of local Japanese clay.“While we were testing the clay, we were informed that it was very similar to Pakistani clay,” Shearer said.The surface got its first serious test in May during the T20 World Cup East Asia-Pacific Qualifier, when six matches were played on the hybrid wicket.The plan was to use the turf wickets for the women’s competition, but heavy rain disrupted the schedule.“The heavy rain a couple of weeks ago upset our plans and we couldn’t get the turf wickets ready in time. But we are confident that the men’s tournament will be held on those wickets,” Shearer said.After October 3, when the men’s final is scheduled to be played, the facility will, in all probability, return to its original identity as a baseball ground for local children.For now, though, the men who transformed it into an Asian Games cricket venue can stand on the sidelines and take pride in what they have created.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Naomi Osaka invested in a $3.1 million hair business after one woman turned her personal salon frustration into a 4-location company
articles.summary: International Sports News: Naomi Osaka has invested in several businesses outside tennis, but one of her more unusual bets came in the haircare industry. In 2024, Osaka became a.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka has invested in several businesses outside tennis, but one of her more unusual bets came in the haircare industry. In 2024, Osaka became an investor in Pressed Roots, a salon company founded by Piersten Gaines for customers with textured hair.The business had already shown signs of traction before Osaka came on board. Pressed Roots had generated $2 million in annual revenue in 2022, followed by $3.5 million in 2023. Gaines then raised $3.1 million from a group that included Osaka, Howard Schultz, Meg Whitman, Slauson & Co. and RevTech Ventures.How Piersten gaines built Pressed Roots around an overlooked customerGaines came up with the idea while studying at Harvard Business School. She had seen how blowout chains such as Drybar offered customers a standard experience, but she struggled to find something similar for textured hair.“I had a lot of really terrible salon experiences throughout my life,” Gaines told Fortune in 2024. She wanted to build a chain where customers could expect trained stylists and a consistent service each time they visited.Before putting money into a permanent location, Gaines tested the idea through pop-ups in Boston, Atlanta and Dallas. The appointments sold out, giving her evidence that customers would pay for the service. She spent about two years running pop-ups before raising $500,000 to open her first permanent location in Dallas.The first salon was scheduled to open in March 2020. Gaines held a soft launch three days before the planned opening, with more than 250 people attending. She said the salon was already booked for its first month before the pandemic forced it to close.That setback did not change the basic business model. Pressed Roots focused on the silk blowout and built its own stylist training programme. Its stylists also work as employees instead of independent contractors, giving the company more control over the customer experience. How Naomi Osaka joined a group of high-profile Pressed Roots investorsThe $3.1 million raise came after Gaines had already shown investors that customers were willing to spend on the service. Inc. reported that Pressed Roots generated about $2 million in revenue in 2022 before reaching $3.5 million the following year.Osaka was not the only prominent name attached to the round. Former HP CEO Meg Whitman and former Starbucks CEO Howard Schultz’s Schultz Family Foundation also invested. Slauson & Co. and RevTech Ventures were among the other backers, while Gaines also connected with angel investors through Slauson & Co.The business had a clear pitch beyond the salon itself. Gaines told Fortune that customers in her target demographic continued spending on their hair even during the pandemic. Her argument to investors was that haircare was not simply an occasional luxury for these customers.“Our goal is to make quality haircare accessible,” Gaines told Fortune.In April 2025, Pressed Roots had four locations and about 200 employees. Gaines was also looking beyond the salons, with plans to expand into hair products and accessories. The company’s Houston expansion had already taken its footprint outside the Dallas-Fort Worth area.The investment therefore came after Gaines had spent years testing the idea, building revenue and proving that a specialised salon could attract a loyal customer base. Osaka joined a wider group of investors backing a business that had already moved from a Harvard classroom idea to a growing Texas-based company.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Simone Biles, leyenda de la gimnasia artística que suma 41 medallas entre Juegos Olímpicos y Mundiales, ha denunciado que tres intrusos enmascarados entraron en su casa de Chicago y robaron su lujoso Porsche GTS valorado en 200.000 euros. La mítica gimnasta de 29 años publicó un vídeo en TikTok para compartir la impactante noticia. "Siento que necesito un coche nuevo porque, durante nuestros últimos meses en Chicago, tres hombres enmascarados entraron en nuestra casa y robaron mi Porsche... Me robaron el GTS. No está claro cuándo ocurrió el robo ni si la Policía ha realizado detenciones, pero Biles confirmó que el vehículo fue recuperado. Poco después Simone Biles publicó otro vídeo comprándose un Lamborghini Urus (valorado en más de 270.000 euros) en un concesionario de Houston. Simone Biles, que vive con su esposo Jonathan Owens (jugador de la NFL que juega en los Indianapolis Colts), confesó que "siento que necesito un programa de telerrealidad". "Las cosas que me pasan son una auténtica locura, así que para los productores sería muy fácil simplemente grabar lo que sucede habitualmente", compartió. Simone Biles, siete veces oro olímpica, desveló que el robo en su casa fue una de las razones por las que ella y Owens adquirieron su nuevo perro dóberman.

articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India's men's skeet team of Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Mairaj Ahmed Khan and Bhavtegh Singh Gill secured the bronze medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
articles.body: India's men's skeet team of Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Mairaj Ahmed Khan and Bhavtegh Singh Gill secured the bronze medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 on Wednesday after prevailing over Kazakhstan in a shoot-off.The Indian trio finished level with Kazakhstan on 346 points in the men's skeet team event, but held their nerve in the shoot-off to finish third and claim the medal.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyNaruka also advanced to the men's skeet individual final after producing a strong performance in qualification. The final is scheduled to begin at 12:30 PM IST.The medal came on a productive day for India in shooting, with the country's men's and women's skeet teams both securing bronze medals. articles.summary: CNAE propone que los usuarios de este medio de transporte reciban formación para evitar multas y accidentes.
articles.body: Tarde o temprano, la necesidad de que los usuarios de patinetes eléctricos reciban formación previa para conocer las normas de circulación y los posibles peligros de su manejo iba a salir a la luz. No solo por las denuncias que acumulan por circular por aceras, ir con auriculares o usar el móvil, sino también por la vulnerabilidad de sus usuarios. Y quien ha hecho esta petición ha sido la Confederación Nacional de Autoescuelas (CNAE), que ha pedido a las administraciones que apuesten por esta medida como solución preventiva para evitar accidentes. Lo que las autoescuelas proponen es que estos miles y miles de usuarios reciban formación previa en sus centros, aunque nada han dicho sobre si sería conveniente reclamar un posible examen que evaluaría su aprovechamiento del curso. Así, una formación sobre señales y normas de circulación, además de un conocimiento sobre los riesgos reales de este medio de transporte, quitaría peso a las acciones actuales, que se basan en vigilar y sancionar las infracciones a unas normas que muchos usuarios desconocen porque nadie les ha exigido que las conozcan. Esta formación incidiría también formación en los peligros que entrañan las drogas cuando se manejan estos patinetes, ya que solo en 2025 se tramitaron 60.492 expedientes administrativos por drogas y la tendencia de este consumo sigue al alza. En líneas generales, el curso que proponen ofrecer se inspiraría en los que ya reciben los conductores que han perdido puntos o el carné de conducir. Y su aplicación está prevista ya en la legislación española, que contempla unos módulos de concienciación vial para futuros conductores que todavía no se han puesto en práctica. Según CNAE, los beneficios de los actuales cursos de recuperación de puntos respaldan esta petición, ya que "muchos de quienes los hacen se preguntan por qué no recibieron esta formación antes de empezar a conducir", y si después, cuando ya se ha dado positivo, se ha cometido un delito o se ha sufrido un accidente. Quien tiene que dar el visto bueno a estos cursos de formación es la propia DGT y las administraciones competentes, con quienes CNAE se compromete a desarrollar estos cursos formativos y preventivos de manera inmediata. Pero, de momento, desde Tráfico no se han pronunciado al respecto.
