articles.title: Newcastle’s January Focus Is Targeting A Centre Back & Right Winger
articles.summary: Ross Wilson and Matthias Jaissle are prioritizing youth as the Magpies eye a squad refresh to secure long-term defensive stability and dynamic new options ou...
articles.body:
Newcastle United have already begun looking beyond the opening months of the season, with the club reportedly identifying two key positions to target when the January transfer window opens.

A young centre-back and a right-sided forward are understood to have emerged as priorities for the Magpies as sporting director Ross Wilson, head coach Matthias Jaissle and the club's recruitment department continue to shape the next phase of Newcastle's squad rebuild.

The reported recruitment priorities come after a summer of significant change at St James' Park. Newcastle adopted a noticeably younger recruitment strategy, bringing in players with development potential as the club looks to build a squad capable of competing at the highest level over the longer term.

That philosophy is expected to continue into 2027, although there is currently no indication that Newcastle are guaranteed to complete deals in both positions during January.

Defensive recruitment appears to be particularly important given the age profile of some of Newcastle's current options.

Fabian Schär and Dan Burn are both experienced members of the squad, while younger defenders including Sven Botman and Malick Thiaw provide Newcastle with longer-term options. The club's reported interest in another young centre-back would therefore allow Newcastle to begin planning for the future rather than waiting until an immediate need develops.

Schär and Burn have also been identified in reports as players whose long-term futures will need consideration, making succession planning increasingly relevant.

Newcastle have already demonstrated their willingness to invest heavily in young talent, and the recruitment of another centre-back would fit that broader strategy.

The defensive picture has also been affected by injuries during previous periods, highlighting the importance of maintaining sufficient depth across the back line.

The other position reportedly under consideration is a right-sided attacker.

Jacob Murphy remains an important option in the position, while Anthony Elanga can also operate from the right after arriving during Newcastle's summer rebuild. However, with Murphy approaching the latter stages of his current contract, recruitment officials are understood to be considering a younger long-term option.

One name already linked with Newcastle is Sporting CP winger Geny Catamo . Reports have suggested that Newcastle are monitoring the Mozambique international, although no formal offer or advanced negotiations have been reported. Sporting are understood to value Catamo at around €60 million through his release clause.

Whether Catamo ultimately becomes a serious target remains to be seen, with Newcastle expected to continue assessing a number of potential options before deciding where to invest.

The recruitment strategy is also likely to reflect Jaissle's footballing philosophy.

The German head coach has spoken about having a clear idea of his squad while also wanting to assess his players before making further decisions. Newcastle's summer business already reflected an emphasis on youth and potential, with players such as Bazoumana Touré and Sean Steur joining the club.

The latest reports suggest that the same approach will continue.

Rather than simply looking for short-term solutions, Newcastle appear to be planning several windows ahead, with recruitment meetings already being used to identify positions and potential targets for 2027 and beyond.

For Newcastle supporters, the January window could therefore provide an early indication of how the new era under Jaissle and Wilson will develop.

A centre-back and right winger are reportedly the two positions currently receiving particular attention, but much will depend on injuries, performances, contract situations and the availability of suitable targets between now and January.

With the summer rebuild already significantly changing the squad, Newcastle's next recruitment decisions could provide another important step in the club's longer-term plans.

articles.title: Orthopedic surgeon discusses Commanders QB Jayden Daniels' options
articles.summary: What are all of the options for Jayden Daniels as he looks to return to the field?
articles.body:
"Just follow the science" is a familiar refrain in recent years; however, if we learned anything from the pandemic, it is that some science is much clearer than others, and in some areas of science there is not the uniform agreement that the public is often led to believe.

So how about Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels' dislocated elbow ? What is the diagnosis? What is the prognosis? What are the options? And what is the timetable?

Dr. Michael Alaia is a Sports Orthopedic Surgeon at NYU and was a guest on Grant & Danny on 106.7 The Fan Tuesday. Dr. Alaia shared his professional experience and insights on the Commanders quarterback's options and recovery. Daniels extended his left arm to regain his balance as he fell Sunday, and unexpectedly, his elbow moved/dislocated.

Here are some selected quotes from Dr. Alaia's discussion with Grant and Danny.

Keep in mind this is the second dislocation of Daniels' left elbow within the last nine months, and that he was treated without surgery.

"The first thing that runs through my head is that when someone has the same injury on a joint that has been treated without surgery, my worry is that if this doesn't get stabilized, perhaps it might continue to happen...so my biggest fear is that this might be more of a recurring type of injury, at this point, if it is not addressed in a different way, shape, or form."

"I think that many elbow dislocations without significant injuries to the ligaments, bone, or cartilage are treated non-surgically. There have been many athletes that have had elbow dislocations, and they are out for a few weeks. They have a full, uneventful recovery, and they never have a dislocation again. That usually is the norm."

"It would be very rare to subject an athlete to a season-ending surgical procedure to reconstruct ligaments when the great majority of the time the athlete is going to be fine without anything done...But when they start happening more than once, that's when the worries start getting in your head. Okay, maybe we need to start doing something."

"They have to look at the MRI. They have to see if there are any structural damages. See what the ligaments look like, are there any significant tears? Are there any loose bodies or cartilage damage floating around the joint? Are there any fractures etc.?"

"The conversations between the player, the physicians, the training staff, and agents are detailed conversations. They are going to run through every possible outcome here. They are going to go through the gamut of treatment options. At the end of the day, the player makes the decision as to what they would like to do."

"As long as the player is educated about risks and benefits of proceeding either non-surgically or surgically, that's when good medical care is delivered."

"Bracing definitely has been shown to help particularly unstable elbows. There have been players that play in braces if they have evidence of elbow instability. Sometimes surgery is indicated on athletes...it all depends on the symptoms, quality of life, and expectations about the stress through the joint that are going to be (occur)."

articles.title: Felipe Melo – The Head
articles.summary: Some people are born leaders, or become them when the occasion calls for it.At the beginning of his career, Roberto Mancini favoured a purely technical midfi...
articles.body:
Some people are born leaders, or become them when the occasion calls for it.

At the beginning of his career, Roberto Mancini favoured a purely technical midfield. At Inter , too, we saw Figo, Cambiasso , Veron and Stankovic lined up from right to left. Pure creativity, perhaps at the expense of physical presence. Things were different in England, where he developed a footballing admiration for Yaya Tourè . Physical strength and technique, mobility and leadership: in the Ivorian, Mancini saw the midfielder he wanted at the heart of his team.

Felipe Melo was at Galatasaray, the next stop in his career. Here too, the Brazilian became the team's reference point on the pitch, the last man standing. When Mancini returned to Inter, he asked for and secured the signing of the Comandante, as he had by then become known in Turkey: a player who could sometimes be a little too aggressive, but whose temperament and technical qualities were beyond doubt.

Felipe Melo began his Inter career by winning a derby; he managed to keep an Inter side afloat that was certainly not a Scudetto team, but one that dreamt of greater things. They won their first four games and went into their home game against Verona looking to maintain their solo lead. This was an Inter side featuring players who would later win the Club's biggest honours, such as Handanovic, Perisic and Brozovic , as well as many others who remained in the hearts of the fans, including Guarin and Miranda. And then there was Felipe Melo, ready to battle in midfield. At 32, he no longer had the legs he had when he enjoyed a brilliant first Serie A campaign at Fiorentina . Then came his move to Juve, followed by some controversy in hindsight.

That afternoon, he chose Inter vs. Verona to score his only goal in the Nerazzurri shirt, rising imperiously to meet a corner. 1-0 and 15 points from 15.

Inter would finish fourth at the end of the season, but only three Italian teams qualified for the Champions League. The team was still under construction and, a few years later, would return to Europe's top competition and remain there. Melo lost his place in the midfield pecking order after a poor performance against Lazio , in which he conceded the penalty before being sent off, which gave the Biancocelesti a definitive lead. He later returned to Brazil, where he had time to win a Copa Libertadores at the age of 40.

Today, in interviews, Felipe Melo describes himself as a Nerazzurro without a shadow of a doubt. Because you are usually born an Inter fan, but you can also become one along the way.

articles.title: “Were United trying to…”: Paul Scholes questions decision to buy Andrey Santos
articles.summary: 4Manchester United midfielder Andrey Santos has started just two games since joining United this summer from Chelsea. The Red Devils began the transfer windo...
articles.body:
Manchester United midfielder Andrey Santos has started just two games since joining United this summer from Chelsea . The Red Devils began the transfer window in pursuit of Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes , but failed to sign either.

INEOS ultimately made Santos their first signing of the summer, which raised quite a few eyebrows. The Brazilian registered 43 appearances for the Blues last season, scoring three goals and providing four assists.

United also signed Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba before the end of the transfer window to bolster their midfield. The Belgian started alongside Santos in the opening game of the season, which ended in a disastrous 2-0 defeat to Hull City.

Since then, Carrick has preferred the midfield axis of Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo , with the Brazilian mostly appearing from the bench. The player's only other start for the Red Devils came in the 3-2 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion in the EFL Cup third round.

United legend Paul Scholes has now provided his opinion on the player.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Scholes questioned the decision to sign the unproven Santos this summer. He said: "It feels quite sad to say this but Man United are a club now that are not trying to win the league with recruitment."

"Santos, Baleba, they've brought players in that physically they may be better. Santos played 11 games for Chelsea, they paid £50million for him. But he's not getting into the team, now Baleba might make a bit of difference."

The Ginger Prince suggested that the Red Devils should always target players who can win them the Premier League. He added: "But again, if you're recruiting at the start of the season for Manchester United, it should be for players that you think you can go and win the league with. I think they're a million miles away."

"I think they're just trying to consolidate from what Michael did last year, which is hard to get your head around. Were United trying to buy an Elliot Anderson? Probably. Now that's a signing where you think that might help you get a lot better. The players they've bought aren't making them any better."

Carrick will be disappointed with summer business

Scholes went on to insist that Carrick will be disappointed with the transfer business this summer. He continued: "Michael must be really disappointed with what has happened in the summer."

"I reckon behind the scenes he thinks he's been let down. What Michael did last year was very, very good. The most important time for Michael was the start of this season. These games now are where you put a marker down, it gives you a foundation for the rest of the season."

Carrick won 12 of his 17 games in charge last season, but has only managed two wins in seven games this campaign.

While it is easy to label Santos as a panic buy, perhaps it is too early to write him off yet. The Brazilian is still young and, given time and guidance, could turn out to be a smart buy.

articles.title: Mariners fade into fall in 7-0 loss to Astros
articles.summary: Summer is over
articles.body:
The Mariners were pushed to the brink of elimination Tuesday night, losing to the Astros 7-0.

Logan Gilbert never found a rhythm in this one, allowing baserunners to lead off each of the first three innings. Over only four innings of work, Gilbert allowed 10 hits, walked two batters and struck out only three. He avoided disaster in both the first and second, but couldn't perform the escape act a third time, giving up a three-run homer to Christian Walker in the top of the third to open up a larger Astros lead, one that would never be threatened.

"Should have been a little more outside," Gilbert said on the home run pitch to Walker. "It was kind of middle low. Not a great spot. It was 1-0 but still you gotta get it to the spot that we're trying to go to."

Keeping the current rotation, Gilbert would be slated to start in the final game of the season Sunday. When asked about his feelings on making that start, he said, "I mean, that's my job. I love pitching. Like, it's going to be taken away one day. So if I can have the ball, I want it. There's fans showing up that pay their hard-earned money to watch up play, regardless of the situation. So, you know, I owe it to them, to the organization, everybody. But honestly I just love pitching."

The Astros jumped out in front quickly in the top of the first. Jeremy Peña reached with an infield single on a ball that forced J.P. Crawford to dive to his right. After Peña stole second on the first pitch of the next at bat, Yordan Álvarez grounded an RBI single through the right side to drive him in. The next two hitters singled as well to load the bases with nobody out. Despite a rough beginning to his start, Gilbert wiggled his way out of trouble and stopped the bleeding right there. In the process, he struck out Yainer Díaz to pass Mark Langston for fourth on the Mariners' all-time strikeout leaderboard. The Mariners managed a couple of baserunners in the bottom half of the inning and made Cristian Javier labor a bit, but Julio Rodríguez flew out to the warning track to leave the runners stranded. After an inning, the M's trailed only 1-0.

The vibes of this game were gross from the get-go and one of the few moments that commanded my complete attention came on a bungled appeal call in the top of the fourth. Cam Smith never touched first base while avoiding a collision with Josh Naylor , who was attempting to field an errant throw from Brock Rodden. Cal Raleigh , who was backing up on the play, applied a tag to Smith before he could return to the base, and first base umpire Marvin Hudson signaled the runner safe. The Mariners then formally appealed with Gilbert stepping off the rubber and throwing to first, and when Hudson again signaled Smith safe — objectively the wrong call, mind you — Dan Wilson attempted to challenge the call and was denied for taking too long. He came out of the dugout to mount a protest, which convinced the umpires to huddle and discuss it, but they ultimately decided to leave their decision the way it was.

The play didn't end up having consequences — the Mariners did get through the inning unscathed despite an additional base hit by the following hitter — but it is going to allow me to beat the drum about my hatred for the modern appeal play. Hudson gets it wrong on the field twice, though his interpretation of the first tag by Raleigh seems ambiguous; Wilson said Raleigh's first tag during the play was because he thought the runner had made an attempt at second, a separate issue altogether. Either way, the rules allow for challenging a fact-based appeal, and Wilson was denied this opportunity for taking too long to challenge despite making said challenge immediately after attempting the formal appeal. Wilson apparently would've had to submit the challenge after Raleigh's first tag, even though Raleigh was appealing something entirely different with it.

These days, in a fashion that's emblematic of the sport as a whole grappling with its past, the line between archaic appeal play rules and instant replay challenges creates controversy more often than it doesn't. In this case, it resulted in the wrong call being made. If formal appeals are to be encouraged, then teams shouldn't be timed out of challenging incorrect appeal decisions immediately after they are made. MLB should probably find a way to sort out this weird gray area before it rears its ugly head in a more consequential moment.

Anyway, the last three paragraphs were a testament to how uneventful this game was from the Mariners' side of things. I spent multiple innings writing that out and nothing of note happened in the meantime.

In the sixth inning, the Astros tacked on an additional run with a solo homer to left by Isaac Paredes . It was around this time I switched over to the radio to take one of my last opportunities to hear Rick Rizzs, who is finishing up his final year in the booth calling Mariners baseball. I cherished every moment, even as he choked out a dejected call of an Álvarez two-run homer in the eighth to extend the Astros' lead and set the eventual final score. It's been talked about ad nauseam at this point, but one of the true calamities of the 2026 season is Rizzs getting stuck with one of, if not the most disappointing season in franchise history for his swan song. A true injustice.

Tuesday night marked the fall equinox in the Northern Hemisphere, and while the Mariners still need another loss or Rangers win to be officially eliminated from playoff contention, their loss to the Astros might as well have marked an end to summer in the baseball sense as well. The Mariners will not be playing meaningful fall baseball in 2026. For the 44th time in 50 seasons, the Mariners will head inside for the long winter as another team from their division keeps playing.

articles.title: Germany's saviour? How Klopp is looking to turn fortunes around
articles.summary: As Jurgen Klopp prepares for his first game as Germany manager, BBC Sport looks at how is trying to turn their fortunes around.
articles.body:
It has been quite the ride since Jurgen Klopp was announced as Germany's head coach in July.

In his first news conference, Klopp admonished the media, urging them to treat him fairly and refrain from any attacks against his family.

Last Thursday, during another media conference, Klopp called for "positive patriotism" amid political turmoil in the country.

When asked whether he considers himself an ambassador for Germany in his new role, Klopp's answer was a serious one.

"From my perspective as a sportsman, I can say that I would very much like to reclaim the flag for myself, for all of us," said Klopp.

"I want it so that when someone waves it, no-one thinks: 'What is wrong with you?' Instead, I want people to understand: You are happy and realise how lucky you were to be born, grow up, or move to this wonderful country."

His statement was made in light of the success of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. The anti-immigration party has since scored another win in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

Klopp's remarks were widely and positively discussed in the media - the German national team represents a diverse Germany, as several players come from a migrant background.

KIopp also remarked about the recent success of Alexander Zverev at the US Open, the women's basketball team at the European Championship and German athletes at the European Athletics Championships, saying sport can ensure "a sense of community".

He added: "This is our mission: we need to create a good atmosphere."

Klopp knows, intentionally or not, how to make headlines.

However, the German Football Association (DFB) didn't hire the former Liverpool boss on an annual salary of £6m to become a commentator on the state of Germany - but to transform a floundering national team.

Between the two news conferences, Klopp looked like the busiest national team boss on the planet, making countless visits to league games and training facilities.

One day fans could see Klopp sitting in the stands of Dortmund 's Signal Iduna Park, his old stomping ground and, not long after, they may have caught a picture of him in the VIP lounge of Mainz's stadium or somewhere near Eintracht Frankfurt 's training pitch talking to players.

Klopp has approached this new job with open eyes. Initially, the charismatic 59-year-old drew up a list of 57 players who could have been selected for this first international break.

"Players will receive chances who don't even expect it yet," Klopp said in July.

His first selection wasn't short of surprises. In the flavour of a trial-and-error principle, Klopp and his staff decided to select two almost completely different squads for the upcoming four games.

The first squad, including Joshua Kimmich , Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala , will face arch-rivals the Netherlands at Johan Cruyff Arena on Thursday (19:45 BST) and host Greece on Sunday.

The second squad, with Florian Wirtz and Aleksandar Pavlovic, face Serbia at home and Greece on the road in the second half of this international break. The only player who was selected for both is back-up goalkeeper Finn Dahmen.

The selection process means we will not see Germany's best starting XI this time around. Instead, Klopp clearly intends to try out new players, some of whom played in Germany's second tier only a few months ago.

Take, for example, Felix Keidel, a 23-year-old full-back-midfielder hybrid from recently promoted SV Elversberg.

A year ago, Keidel was as far away from the national team as the Oktoberfest from Rio Carnival.

Now Keidel - just like Mika Baur , Bambase Conte, Max Rosenfelder , Philipp Treu , and Vitaly Janelt - has the chance to show he could be a valuable cog in the machine.

Klopp has never built his success merely on star names - he has always taken a liking to undervalued and overlooked players.

He once signed an little-known Polish winger by the name of Lukasz Piszczek and moulded him into one of the best right-backs in Europe who would go toe-to-toe with Cristiano Ronaldo in his prime. And he helped transform Andy Robertson into a force on Liverpool's left side.

Klopp's style helps to elevate all the members of his squad - not just the most talented.

Fitness and mental readiness are highly important, and some newcomers might just have that to impress the new manager.

But man-marking is prevalent in Germany's top flight, while Klopp prefers his teams to close down the player in possession to create superior numbers around the ball. So some of the Bundesliga players will have to adapt quickly.

"It is not important who plays but how someone plays," Klopp said last week. "I expect a lot from the beginning. It could be a bit wild, but I accept that. It just has to be lively."

Klopp has chosen younger squads compared to the ones we saw in the past couple of years. Manuel Neuer , Antonio Rudiger and Pascal Gross have retired from international football, and other 30-somethings might just not receive a chance to get into the team again.

"I think it is about time to wish the new generation best of luck," Gross said after Brighton 's win over Arsenal on Saturday. "I still enjoy playing football here in the club, but there's a change in Germany and rightfully so."

Both squads for this international break have an average age between 24 and 25. Youth and energy seem to be preferred.

"I have the desire to work with guys who cannot wait to wear this jersey, who want to play the kind of football everybody enjoys and who perform even better wearing the national team jersey," Klopp said.

We can expect from him to simplify Germany's approach to ball possession. Predecessor Julian Nagelsmann bent over backwards to hide some of the flaws he detected in his squad and thus created highly complex tactical systems.

On the contrary, Klopp intends to put an emphasis on the wings and break defences there. We saw what he was able to achieve with the likes of Mohamed Salah , Trent Alexander-Arnold and Sadio Mane from wide areas.

While underwhelming at the past couple of international tournaments, Germany still possess a deep talent pool. Cologne's rising star Said El Mala and 18-year-old Bayern Munich talent Lennart Karl will get chances to show their skills on the wings.

Freiburg 's Derry Scherhant and Barcelona 's Karim Adeyemi provide plenty of speed, just like Brentford 's Kevin Schade who has returned to the squad after being left out for the World Cup. There is potential for an exciting Germany side we have not seen in quite a while.

Finally, the emotional component plays a role in Klopp's entire approach. He works towards a fresh start for the national team and a new spirit in the country.

Last Thursday, he wore a cap that read "One of 83 million". It was a clear indication he wants to unite all 83 million Germans behind this team and they are all in it together.

Klopp has spent plenty of time thus far attempting to shape narratives off the field - but now the spotlight turns to his ability to get the best out of his group of players on the pitch.

articles.title: Truro City progress after rare FA Cup victory
articles.summary: Truro City manager John Askey hopes his side can continue to progress in the FA Cup after their first win in the competition in five years.
articles.body:
Truro City manager John Askey hopes his side can continue to progress in the FA Cup after getting their first win in the competition in five years.

The Tinners beat National League North side Merthyr Town 2-0 in their second qualifying round replay at the Truro Community Stadium.

It ensured a third qualifying round tie at home to Hellenic League Premier Division side Cirencester Town - the ninth-tier outfit upset Truro's National League South rivals Farnham Town with a 2-1 win in their replay on Tuesday night.

"It's a great competition and obviously the further you can go then obviously it creates a lot of interest in the football club," Askey told BBC Radio Cornwall.

"We'll hopefully go as far as we possibly can and we've got a draw at home against a team who are obviously in a couple of leagues below, so it's a great opportunity to progress, but we want to take it wider."

Truro had not won an FA Cup tie since they beat Exmouth Town in the first qualifying round in the 2021-22 competition.

They needed an equaliser deep in stoppage time in Wales on Saturday to stay in the competition and Merthyr started the replay well, controlling the opening quarter of the game.

But the hosts went ahead thanks to a 25th-minute Will Dean penalty after his brother Tom had been brought down in the box.

The goal ignited Truro's confidence and Askey's side created a number of chances before Ben Starkie scored his first competitive goal for the club seven minutes after half-time to secure Askey's first FA Cup victory as Truro boss.

"The longer the game went I thought it was only going to be one winner," added Askey.

"It was good play leading up to the penalty and Tom Dean's done really well.

"Getting one in front changes the game and I think from then on we've got the momentum and they never seemed to get another foothold in the game."

But Askey was quick to warn against any complacency for Truro in the next round.

The club has made the first round proper just once in their history - back in 2017 - but while the chance to face a side three leagues below them is a good opportunity, it is one he says they cannot take lightly.

"To get drawn at home is a big plus for us," he said.

"We've got to be aware that it's a great opportunity for us, but they'll be trying to cause a cup upset, as we're hoping to do if we get further.

"If you're not at it, no matter who you play against, then you can come unstuck in the cup, but we'll enjoy tonight and then we'll think about that when it comes along."

articles.title: Jaxson Dart’s injury ends dreams of devastating partnership at the Giants, tough decision coming up
articles.summary: The clouds of doom and gloom are setting over the New York Giants, and the toughest decision with Jaxson Dart’s injury is yet to arrive. The early-season opt...
articles.body:
The clouds of doom and gloom are setting over the New York Giants, and the toughest decision with Jaxson Dart's injury is yet to arrive.

The early-season optimism after the first game around the New York Giants evaporated just as quickly as it emerged, as Jaxson Dart suffered an injury in the second game.

The Giants went off the rails in a loss to the LA Rams, and the bad news kept coming thereafter, as Dart is supposedly out for the season, as per the latest prognosis.

This is the worst-case scenario for the Giants as it ends the dream of a potentially devastating partnership. Instead, it is replaced by the spectre of a tough decision.

New York Giants had something in Jaxson Dart and Malik Nabers

For a team that hasn't enjoyed the greatest success in the last few years, the draft becomes their only hope of landing potential superstars.

That was the case with the New York Giants, who last won the Super Bowl in 2011, and finished bottom of the standings for the last two years.

Therefore, when they drafted Jaxson Dart in 2025, the hope was rekindled, especially because WR Malik Nabers was already showing signs of being a capable contributor.

The Dart-Nabers partnership had devastating potential, but if Dart misses this season through injury, the duo will have had just 68 snaps together in two years of being on the same team.

That is not what anyone would have foreseen when Dart was drafted and Nabers was looking good, but a combination of injuries to both Nabers and Dart is making that nightmare a reality.

Even when Dart returns, their two young hopes will have both recovered from ACL injuries, as Nabers picked up this issue in Week 4 of last season. Can they really come back from such an issue at the same level as before?

Tough decision awaits the New York Giants

Barring a spectacular return to form for backup QB Jameis Winston, Dart's injury news probably condemns the Giants to another bottom place in the standings.

Then comes the tough decision for the front office. Do they invest in another young QB in the draft or hitch their wagon to Dart's return and his partnership with Nabers working out as planned?

The sample size is simply too small to make an informed decision in the draft, and this level of uncertainty hurts team planning immensely.

The Giants will have to hit a bullseye with their Dart because their QB Dart will have spent most of his time with the team on the sidelines.

articles.title: Freeman eyes rest as Dodgers close in on first round bye
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers are five games from the end of the regular season, and for all the noise surrounding October, Freddie Freeman knows there is still...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers are five games from the end of the regular season, and for all the noise surrounding October, Freddie Freeman knows there is still something worth chasing before the postseason begins.

The Dodgers took another step toward getting it Tuesday night.

With Freeman driving in three runs, the offense continuing its late-season surge and eight pitchers combining on a shutout, the Dodgers rolled past the San Diego Padres , 7-0, inm front of 46,066 at Uniqlo Field at Dodger Stadium.

The win moved the Dodgers to 97-60, its 15th victory in its last 18 games, and kept the Dodgers one game behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League with five games remaining.

The division has already been secured. The Padres, meanwhile, still have plenty at stake, with Tuesday's loss leaving San Diego in a three-way tie for the final two National League Wild Card spots.

For the Dodgers, the immediate target is simpler: one more win.

One more win would secure a first-round bye and give a roster that has endured its share of injuries and late-season wear a chance to breathe before the postseason begins.

Freeman made clear afterward how much that opportunity means.

"I feel like we've just been playing really good baseball as a group lately as well," Freeman said. "So we had to step up when guys went down, and that's a credit to the guys that have been going. But you want to be playing well going into the playoffs. We do. We need one more win for that bye."

And then, Freeman added, comes the part the Dodgers have been waiting for.

"Get some rest, and then have a great week of practicing going into the playoffs," he said. "But just swinging the bats at the right time. Hopefully, we can carry that."

The Dodgers' offense needed only two innings to turn Tuesday's game.

The four-run second inning began with two outs. Teoscar Hernández and Josue De Paula singled, and then Andy Pages , returning to the lineup after missing roughly four weeks with a fractured hand, was hit by a pitch on the left shoulder to load the bases.

Michael King began to unravel. The Padres right-hander walked Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts consecutively, allowing the Dodgers to score their first two runs without another hit.

Then Freeman did what he has done throughout his career. He brought the runs home. Freeman lined a single into center field, scoring Edman and Pages to make it 4-0.

In the fourth, Betts opened the inning with a ground-rule double. Freeman followed with another line drive, this one an RBI single to center, extending the Dodgers' lead to 5-0.

Freeman finished 2-for-4 with three RBIs.

The production came during a stretch in which he has been trying to make adjustments at the plate and find something that feels right with his swing.

"I mean, it's a little better," Freeman said. "I'm just happy I got hits when I needed to get hits today. The last couple of games have been a lot better, so hopefully, we're trending in the right direction when we need to."

The Dodgers have spent much of the season dealing with injuries, inconsistent stretches and players trying to find their rhythm. Now, with October approaching, the lineup is beginning to look more like the group the Dodgers envisioned.

"Kyle's been great. Teo has been hot," Freeman said. "Guys are starting to come back that we've been missing over the last couple weeks too. So good to see Andy back. You know Shohei coming back tomorrow. So a lot of good things happening for the offense lately."

The Dodgers are getting healthy at the right time

Pages' return was one of the night's biggest developments.

After missing the previous four weeks, Pages was back in the lineup and reached base twice, going 0-for-2 with a walk and a hit by pitch.

"Super happy to be back on the field," Pages said.

Asked how long he has been pain-free while working his way back from the fractured hand, Pages answered simply.

The Dodgers also activated Roki Sasaki , who made his return to the mound and threw one scoreless inning. Sasaki allowed two hits, struck out two and threw 20 pitches. He had originally been told he might pitch two innings, but the pitch count changed those plans.

"I was actually told to probably go two innings," Sasaki said, "but because maybe my pitch count got very high so I figured it would end up being just one inning."

Sasaki was also asked about the possibility of returning to a late-inning role during the postseason after having experience in that role previously.

"I'm just gonna try to make the most of every opportunity I'm given," Sasaki said.

The Dodgers did not need a traditional starting pitcher to shut down the Padres.

Instead, Dave Roberts deployed eight pitchers in a bullpen game, and the group responded by holding the Padres scoreless. Brock Stewart opened the game before Justin Wrobleski , Blake Treinen , Sasaki, Edwin Díaz , Kyle Hurt , Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer followed. Together, they kept the Padres off the scoreboard while the Dodgers' offense continued piling on.

Edman added to the lead in the sixth inning when he launched his eighth home run of the season, driving a 96-mph sinker from Wandy Peralta out of the park.

Will Smith provided the final blow in the seventh, hitting his 10th homer of the season to make it 7-0.

It was the type of complete performance the Dodgers have been looking for as the regular season winds down.

The offense is producing. Players are returning. The pitching staff is finding ways to cover innings.

And the Dodgers are one victory away from earning the opportunity Freeman keeps emphasizing. A week off.

The headline Tuesday belonged to Freeman.

On Wednesday, it will belong to Shohei Ohtani.

Dave Roberts said Ohtani will be activated from the 15-day injured list and return to the Dodgers' lineup against the Padres, giving the Dodgers another significant piece for the final five games of the regular season.

Roberts said he is still deciding who will lead off when Ohtani returns, with the decision likely to depend on the opposing pitching matchup.

The expected approach: Ohtani against right-handed pitching and Betts against left-handers.

The timing could hardly be more important. The Dodgers already have the division. They are chasing the top seed.

Freeman's message Tuesday was clear: the Dodgers aren't simply trying to finish the regular season. They are trying to enter October as healthy as possible.

articles.title: Juho Piiparinen headlines impressive Golden Knights in shootout win over Sharks
articles.summary: SAN JOSE—The Vegas Golden Knights and San Jose Sharks competing always makes for compelling action on the ice, especially with the latter being hailed as a t...
articles.body:
SAN JOSE—The Vegas Golden Knights and San Jose Sharks competing always makes for compelling action on the ice, especially with the latter being hailed as a team on the rise and the volatile elements that have recently been added on both sides.

However, in this preseason exhibition, the rivalry was secondary in the mind of 18-year-old defenseman Juho Piiparinen.

The first-round pick of the Golden Knights in June after the fallout of the Pavel Dorofeyev trade with the New York Rangers , Piiparinen was given his opportunity to show the Golden Knights coaching staff the type of player they invested in. While the defenseman has played against grown men in his native Finland, and likely will continue to do so once training camp concludes, the NHL experience will always find ways to be vastly different.

However, Piiparinen was up for the challenge, making a number of plays against some of the NHL-caliber talent he was put up against and aiding the Golden Knights in their 2-1 victory over their rival.

The first two periods were controlled by San Jose for the most part, which was an unsurprising development due to the Sharks playing more of their regular NHL lineup.

However, not only did Piiprinen stay ready, but Carter Hart was also able to make some key saves when the defense broke down in front of him. He matched up well against Sharks goaltender Yaroslav Askarov , pulling off impressive stops against the likes of Michael Misa and Collin Graf .

However, the Sharks would finally break through on the power play after Joe Fleming was called for elbowing. After Hart got the best of him all game, Misa finally got his opportunity when a puck bounced off of Vegas defenseman Antti Tuomisto and landed on his stick, giving San Jose the first lead in a hard-fought battle.

However, the Golden Knights would get their fair share of chances throughout the game, with Jackson Hallum getting good chances for the second straight preseason outing.

However, it would be a reclamation project in Alexander Holtz making the difference. His line with Tanner Laczynski and Jonas Rondbjerg was Vegas' most impressive on both ends of the ice, but Holtz would get a one-timer off with Braeden Bowman getting to the front of the net.

Piiparinen would then make his finest play of the night, stopping a play between two of San Jose's best forwards in Tyler Toffoli and Igor Chernyshov to preserve the tie and force overtime.

After Hart would make more key saves during the overtime period, the Golden Knights would wind up going to the shootout. Despite starting goals from Matyas Sapovaliv and Ivar Stenberg for both teams, Bowman would finish the job after getting a shot through Askarov's five-hole, followed by Hart stonewalling Chernyshov and Luca Cagnoni to give Vegas the win.

Hart deserved the first star of the game with his performance, stopping 28 of 29 San Jose shots for a stellar .966 save percentage.

The Golden Knights now head into friendlier confines for the remainder of the preseason, returning to T-Mobile Arena to face the Utah Mammoth on Thursday and finishing the slate against these same Sharks on Saturday.

articles.title: 3 bold predictions for Astros vs. Rangers AL West race
articles.summary: The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers enter the final five games tied atop the American League West at 78-79. The Astros reached that point with a win Tuesday...
articles.body:
The Houston Astros and Texas Rangers enter the final five games tied atop the American League West at 78-79. The Astros reached that point with a win Tuesday, while the Rangers lost. Neither club has secured a postseason berth. The loser of the AL West race may need help to reach October through the AL Wild Card.

The standings show a tie, but the teams do not start on equal footing. The Astros won nine of their 13 meetings with the Rangers and own the head-to-head tiebreaker. If they finish with matching records, the Astros take the division. The Rangers must finish at least one game ahead. Every result now affects the division and Wild Card races.

The schedule gives both clubs an opening. The Astros visit the Seattle Mariners once more, then play four road games against the Athletics . The Rangers host the New York Mets twice before facing the Minnesota Twins three times away from home. Here are three predictions for the finish.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Astros will win four of their last five games

Predicting a 4-1 finish for the Astros requires looking beyond their recent form. Houston went 3-7 in their last 10 games and lost their AL West lead before Tuesday. A single win over Seattle did not fix those problems, especially for an offense that has struggled to give its pitchers consistent support.

Still, the remaining opponents make a rebound credible. The Mariners enter Wednesday at 73-84, and the Athletics stand at 62-95. The Astros own a 39-37 road record, so spending the final week away from home does not automatically make their path harder. Four games against the Athletics give the Astros room to recover even if they drop Wednesday's finale in Seattle.

I expect the Astros to win three of four against the Athletics and beat the Mariners once more. That produces an 82-80 finish. It would demand sharper at-bats than Houston showed during its 3-7 slide, particularly when games tighten in late innings.

The Rangers will match Houston's finish and still lose the West

The Rangers have the stronger recent form at 6-4 over their last 10 games. They also get two more games at home, where they have gone 44-35. Winning both against the Mets would put them in a strong position before the final trip to Minnesota.

The challenge comes after they leave Arlington. The Rangers have gone 34-44 on the road, and three of their five remaining games take place at the Twins' ballpark. That split should matter more than the Minnesota's losing record. Texas needs two wins in the series with the Twins. Those wins must come where the Rangers have struggled most , with the division undecided.

Josh Jung and Nathan Eovaldi returned from the injured list this month, giving the club more options for the stretch run. Corey Seager remains central to the Rangers' offense. They have enough talent to win two of three in Minnesota, but their away record makes a sweep harder to predict.

My call is two wins over the Mets and two over the Twins. Texas finishes 82-80, exactly where I expect the Astros to land . Houston's 9-4 season-series advantage would decide the division. A four-win closing stretch would feel strong for the Rangers, yet it would not be enough.

The Rangers will miss the playoffs despite finishing above .500

Losing the AL West would leave Texas chasing the final Wild Card rather than celebrating its 82nd win. Entering Wednesday, the Chicago White Sox held that spot at 81-76. The Cleveland Guardians led Chicago by one game in the AL Central at 82-75. The other two Wild Card spots already look secure. The division's runner-up could therefore face a difficult target.

For the Rangers, the problem is time. Even four wins in five games would produce only 82 victories. Chicago needs two wins in its final five to reach 83, while Cleveland needs just one. Both clubs would have to stumble for an 82-win Texas team to remain in the Wild Card picture.

This is the consequence that makes the tiebreaker so important. Houston can match Texas across the final five games and still take the AL West. The Rangers can play well, finish above .500 and have no postseason place to show for it.

I predict both rivals close 4-1, finish 82-80 and force the standings tiebreaker. The Astros take the division on their head-to-head record. The Rangers' season ends because the Wild Card chase demands more wins than a late surge can supply.

articles.title: (Video) Will Wright scores phenomenal goal on night of high drama for Liverpool U21s
articles.summary: An incredible solo goal from Will Wright was the highlight of a dramatic night for Liverpool under-21s against Rochdale in the Jersey Mike’s Trophy on Tuesda...
articles.body:
An incredible solo goal from Will Wright was the highlight of a dramatic night for Liverpool under-21s against Rochdale in the Jersey Mike's Trophy on Tuesday night.

After Mor Talla Ndiaye was sent off for the Reds and Devante Rodney put the hosts in front at the Crown Oil Arena, Wright equalised in spectacular fashion shortly before half-time.

Two goals from Ian Henderson put the Dale in a commanding position, but stoppage-time goals from Ben Trueman and Josh Sonni-Lambie forced a penalty shootout that Rob Page's side won 7-6 to secure a bonus point .

Wright scores phenomenal solo goal v Rochdale

The manner in which the two points were gained was newsworthy enough even without the majestic goal from Wright.

Gaining possession on the left wing just inside Rochdale's half of the pitch, the 18-year-old surged towards the edge of the penalty area, where he cut inside an off-balance Edward Francis and somehow retained possession in a congested space before curling an exquisite shot past Sam Waller for the coup de grâce.

(Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Another step closer to a first-team debut for Wright?

The highly-rated youngster has already served notice of his marvellous finishing ability in previous games for the under-21s and enjoyed some impressive cameos for the first team in pre-season.

That goal at Rochdale tops the lot, though, and has garnered much wider attention than this competition would usually receive outside of the teams involved.

Wright spoke during the summer about his ambitions to become Liverpool's starting centre-forward in the future, and he showed last night that he can conjure up moments of magic against senior opposition.

He's yet to officially debut for the Reds' first team, and an eventual debut for Andoni Iraola 's side would most likely come in one of the domestic cups rather than a big Premier League or Champions League night.

However, his exploits against Rochdale could potentially expedite his pathway, especially if he can back it up in forthcoming matches for the under-21s.

articles.title: Why Kelsey Mitchell compared Caitlin Clark to LeBron James after their first game together
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell opened up about her first game alongside Caitlin Clark in the 2024 WNBA preseason. Mitchell joined the Fever in 2018, two...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Kelsey Mitchell opened up about her first game alongside Caitlin Clark in the 2024 WNBA preseason.

Mitchell joined the Fever in 2018, two years before Caitlin Clark joined the Iowa Hawkeyes and embarked on one of the greatest NCAA women's basketball careers of all time.

Six years later, Mitchell saw Clark get drafted to be her teammate in the 2024 WNBA Draft, a watershed moment in the league's history as it transformed overnight after Clark joined.

Kelsey Mitchell compares Caitlin Clark's rookie stardom to LeBron James

Mitchell spoke about her first Fever preseason game alongside Clark in a recent interview and compared the attention she received to what LeBron James would.

"I think CC, when she first got here and we had to go play the preseason game in Iowa, I was like, bro, this is like some LeBron —-. I couldn't believe it. To see the lights, the people, and the stuff, I am in awe of CC all the time because she handled it so well. Her as a professional too, she wants to be great."

Mitchell has thrived in her three seasons alongside Clark on the Fever, posting career-highs in each successive season.

Her first season with Clark saw her average 19.2 points, which went up to 20.2 points last season with Clark missing most of the year due to injuries.

This season is an unquestioned peak, as Mitchell is averaging 25.0 points while Clark is averaging 22.8 points and 8.5 assists.

They solidified their status as the greatest scoring duo in WNBA regular-season history, and will be hoping to make a deep run in the 2026 playoffs to establish their credentials as postseason players.

If Clark's regular-season games are regularly breaking records, playoff games with her might be among the most-viewed WNBA games of all time, even challenging records set before the 2000s.

articles.title: ‘They’re going to break our backs’ – Raphinha’s referee complaints revealed after Barcelona beat Sevilla
articles.summary: The Brazilian wanted some protection from the match official.
articles.body:
Raphinha 's chats with match referee Juan Martínez Munuera during Barcelona's win over Sevilla have been revealed and show the Brazilian was asking the match official to keep an eye on the hosts.

Barcelona ran out 3-1 winners at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan , with Raphinha continuing his excellent form with a hat-trick.

Raphinha led by example but also tried to help out his team by asking the referee for some protection in footage captured by ref cam and then broadcast on DAZN.

"Try to be careful with the blocking and grabbing because they're going to break our backs," Raphinha told the referee.

"Yes, we're keeping an eye on it, and in fact, we've seen it, and I've told them as well," Martínez Munuera replied.

Raphinha then said: "Just be careful, because as soon as you call one or two fouls, they're going to stop doing this."

There's also another incident when the referee warns Raphinha and Youssouf Fofana to stop tangling at a free kick: "Fofana, eh, Rapha, Rapha. Listen, both of you, he grabs and so do you. That's not football, that's not football, that's called judo."

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham reveals her family’s financial past, shares advice for building wealth
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham recently explained her approach to money, and the way her family’s background shaped her attitudes towards building wealth. As her populari...
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham recently explained her approach to money, and the way her family's background shaped her attitudes towards building wealth.

As her popularity continues to grow, Sophie Cunningham is likely finding more financial opportunities than ever before. Her estimated $3 million net worth could grow exponentially in the coming years.

The Indiana Fever star has been a role player at the WNBA level for most of her career. However, as of September 2026, she can claim to have one of the biggest fanbases in sports.

In a recent interview she did with the Indiana Fever's social media teams at her family's farm, Cunningham spoke candidly about her family's financial past, and her own ideas for building wealth.

Sophie Cunningham says her family had 'some really good times and really low times' financially

Cunningham is the daughter of two former student athletes. Her father Jim, played football at the University of Missouri, while her mother Paula, was a javelin thrower.

Her father worked as a building contractor, a business which was significantly impacted by the 2008 housing market crash. Cunningham opened up about it in the interview.

"Our family was in the house market when it crashed in 2008 and that was really hard on our family," Cunningham said. "We've had some really good times. We've had some very, very low times.

"I think sometimes when you see both sides of it, sometimes you can be really risky with your money. Sometimes you need to be a little more conservative with your money."

Sophie spoke about how being involved with the farm is really grounding however, and how it helps her chill when it comes to various financial pressures.

Sophie Cunningham says people should 'learn along the way' while taking help from others when it comes to finances

Like many other star athletes, Cunningham now has financial advisors who help her grow her wealth. She explained how much she trusts them and how important that is.

However, the Fever star's advice went beyond that. She encouraged people to learn about how everything works and how they can get involved, too.

"Yes, you have people that are working for you, that are handling your money. But also, learn along the way," the 30-year-old said.

"You can find anything. You can go to the library and find books on it. You can get on social media and there are people to help you there. Finding someone that you feel good about it is the most important thing.

"Everyone is going to be different. I think that's the beautiful thing. It's not one thing to be successful with your money. There's always going to be people who have been where you're at that can help you."

This is excellent advice from the WNBA star. Even regular people, not just athletes, can learn from it. As she continues to build her own wealth, it is clear that Cunningham has a plan for her future.

articles.title: It's clear, Liverpool have signed an incredible African star
articles.summary: Liverpool have signed an absolute gem, it's now becoming official. The Reds have been busy over the course of the last 12 months. We've seen a real generatio...
articles.body:
Liverpool have signed an absolute gem, it's now becoming official.

The Reds have been busy over the course of the last 12 months. We've seen a real generational change occur at Anfield. Liverpool's team have been reshaped, and remoulded.

We've seen legends leave the club. Mo Salah and Andy Robertson most notably this summer but we've also seen new younger players coming in hoping to make their mark on the team.

Change is never easy. Things are never going to work out straight away. However, there are signs that Liverpool are heading in the right direction.

Andoni Iraola has restored the club's identity and Liverpool are once again playing the kind of football that you expect to see at Anfield.

It will take time, for things to be perfect but the Reds are on their way.

The most notable change has been how many U23 players Liverpool have signed over the last year or so.

The Reds are very focused on bringing in players not just for the now but for the future as well. Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet are great example of this.

But also Hugo Ekitike , Florian Wirtz , Milos Kerkez and Bradley Barcola are all players who will form the backbone of this team for many years to come.

Behind them Liverpool are also making some strong additions at youth level. They've signed the likes of Armin Pecsi, Will Wright, Lucca Brughmans, Ifeanyi Ndukwe and Djylian N'Guessan, who all have the potential to be playing for the first-team in the future.

And there's another who has officially confirmed he is a super talent.

Liverpool new signing Mor Talla Ndiaye is incredible

The Reds signed an 18-year-old defender from the Senegalese second division in January. Ndiaye may have caught the eye at the U17 World Cup but his arrival raised a lot of eyebrows.

Liverpool don't tend to sign players directly from Africa. The last time the Reds brought someone in directly from the continent was Taiwo Awoniyi , many years ago.

But Ndiaye's signing is officially becoming a genius one, and it's very apparent that Liverpool have acquired an absolute sensation.

This season the 18-year-old has been incredible for the club's U21 side. Ndiaye has put in some really strong performances both at U21 and U19 level.

He is not only a great defender but he is fantastic on the ball. The fact that he is left-footed makes him a real unicorn. At 18, he's a special talent, and someone who will provide a brilliant option for Iraola's side in the near future.

articles.title: Launch week, day two: Instituto Leão do Mar focuses on Santos
articles.summary: Santos FC began the second day of the launch of the Leão do Mar Institute this Tuesday (22) with a tree-planting event in the Vila Belmiro neighborhood of Sa...
articles.body:
Santos FC began the second day of the launch of the Leão do Mar Institute this Tuesday (22) with a tree-planting event in the Vila Belmiro neighborhood of Santos. The event inaugurated a green roundabout on Rua Mariz e Barros, in the presence of Santos FC vice-president Fernando Bonavides and administrative manager Luiz Fernando Vella, deputy mayor Audrey Kleys, ambassador Christiane Torloni, Leão do Mar Institute finance director Antilia Reis, and the secretary of Environment, Urban Development and Sustainability, Glaucus Renzo. Female and male youth academy athletes, the Club's organized supporter groups, students from UME Professora Emília Maria Reis, and mascots Leo and Baleião were also present.

"The inauguration of the Leão do Mar Institute is a major step for Santos FC. This week highlights our commitment to social and environmental responsibility, and bringing all of this together with the Club's city, in a space so close to our stadium, in the Vila Belmiro neighborhood, also shows the value we place on the community around us that lives Santos FC day by day. Here we have residents, children, and wildlife that will be positively affected by actions like this," said Luiz Fernando Vella, administrative manager of Santos FC.

"This initiative makes us see life in a different way, telling everyone: 'You are also part of society and need to take responsibility for caring for the environment.' We do this through actions like this one, which bring society together, connect with education, and ensure it is present in the birth of new life. As a result, our students will have a greater sense of responsibility in caring for nature. As a Santos supporter, I am even prouder of our team for this social responsibility. As deputy mayor, my heart overflows with joy," added Audrey Kleys, deputy mayor of Santos.

In addition to the tree-planting program, the Club also took part in the inauguration of a new court at UME Professora Emília Maria Reis, in front of the green roundabout, with the special presence of Eternal Idols Abel and Lalá. The school will take part in maintaining the planting site, introducing ecological education to children through contact with nature.

"The children will grow together with the plants. They will take care of this space, which will be a small pocket orchard. If this attitude is nurtured, it grows like that bean seed we used to plant at school. We have lost that sense of wonder, and we want to recover it. But only education can do that. The idea of forest citizenship says that nature is not competitive, but cooperative — if one plant is attacked, all of them are at risk as well. So there is a whole network protecting that space, and that is a lesson for all of us," said Christiane Torloni, ambassador of the Leão do Mar Institute.

Glaucus Renzo, Santos's secretary of Environment, Urban Development and Sustainability, also highlighted the importance of the initiative. "The Institute is an arm that represents society. These social actions at its launch already demonstrate that, and the image of Santos FC amplifies everything. It gives scale to what we see as our shared mission: reintroducing nature into the city. Santos is highly urbanized and vertical, and it needs more trees and more Atlantic Forest. With this planting, we removed asphalt and returned a permeable area to the city, enriching life for everyone,"

articles.title: Nailah Randle shines as Harlan outlasts Brennan to move into first in 29-6A
articles.summary: Randle notched 23 kills as the Hawks won a hotly contested five-set match to break a tie atop the district standings with the Bears.
articles.body:
Harlan's Nailah Randle put on a dominant performance, and the Hawks needed every bit of it against Brennan on Tuesday at Northside Sport Gym.

Randle notched 23 kills in leading Harlan to a grueling five set win over Brennan, 25-17, 22-25, 26-24, 16-25, 15-10, in a match between the top two teams in District 29-6A.

With the win, Harlan (22-10, 8-0) moved into first place in the District 29-6A standings ahead of Brennan (27-7, 7-1), capping off the first round of district competition.

Randle, a 6-1 senior outside hitter and LSU commit, said she knew she would have to step up her game against a Brennan squad which fought to the end, despite missing two key players because of injuries.

"I just wanted to work for my team and produce for my team," Randle said. "I knew it was a big game. So, I just wanted to be able to get the job done for my team."

Harlan coach Monica Gonzales said her team was able to find a way to grind out the win over a tough Brennan squad.

"It was really a great match," Gonzales said. "They're a great team. They work hard; they have really good kids. We just kind of chipped away. We talked about our first contact and it fell apart in our fourth set, but we just regrouped and played hard and that's what's important."

Randle was part of a well-balanced Harlan attack that included senior right side hitter Leeanna Hamilton, a Tulsa commit who contributed 15 kills, and Holly Sieh, a senior outside hitter who added eight kills.

"They (Randle and Hamilton) came out and played hard," Gonzales said. "They've been a part of the program, they've been on varsity for four years. They've known the process; it's ingrained in them. They came up when we needed them, whether it was blocking, whether it was passing, whether it was obviously the kills. But they came to play and they understood that. They're our leaders."

Brennan coach Melissa Dahle said her squad had to make adjustments to counteract Randle's athleticism.

"Nailah's amazing," Dahle said. "Her contact point is above us and that is what it is. We made some blocking adjustments, we made some defensive adjustments and we made some plays on them. I mean Nailah is going to get her kills, and we knew that coming into the game. She is a great player."

Despite having two of their starters and team captains, seniors Aviana Contreras and Mia Nunez, out with injuries, Dahle said was proud of her squad's effort.

"Harlan is a great team," Dahle said. "We have some kids out right now. So, we are in a new lineup, making new adjustments. Kids stepped up that haven't got a lot of playing time this year, so I'm very proud of the way we played. Harlan is a well-coached team so I knew they would come out swinging."

Senior outside hitter Kayla Rodriguez led Brennan with 15 kills, while Adele Ponce notched 10 kills and Kiersten Rodriguez, Kayla's twin sister, added six.

Harlan overcame a slow start in the first set, going on a 6-4 run to take a 9-7 advantage and finishing the frame on a 15-7 run to close it out. Hamilton and middle hitter Aryana Waluk each got two kills in the decisive run.

Brennan got off the mat by winning the second set 25-22 behind the play of the Rodriguez sisters, who had key kills in the latter part of the frame, and an ace from Khloe Cisneros.

Harlan regained the momentum in the third set, as the Hawks got out to a quick lead before Brennan came back to tie it at 14-14. But Randle picked Harlan up, closing out the frame with four kills as the Hawks pulled out a 26-24 win.

Brennan answered again in the see-saw affair, as the Bears got out to a 12-5 lead in the fourth set before winning the frame 25-16. Kayla Rodriguez led the way with seven kills in the set.

In the decisive fifth set, Harlan got out to a 6-2 lead and held on for a 15-10 win in the frame as Randle notched three of the final four kills for the Hawks. Camyrn Batts ended the match with an ace, one of three she served in the match.

The win helped Harlan avenge a two-set loss to Brennan in the Pieper Tournament in August.

Both teams start the second round of district Friday as Harlan hopes to extend its four-game winning streak when the Hawks take on Stevens. Brennan looks to bounce back against Taft.

articles.title: Red Bull confirms Isack Hadjar to stay as Verstappen's F1 teammate in 2027
articles.summary: Isack Hadjar is staying with Red Bull as Max Verstappen's teammate for 2027 after the team extended his contract.  The confirmation Wednesday comes as Hadjar...
articles.body:
BAKU, Azerbaijan (AP) — Isack Hadjar is staying with Red Bull as Max Verstappen's teammate for 2027 after the team extended his contract.

The confirmation Wednesday comes as Hadjar prepares to return to action at this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing three Formula 1 rounds with a wrist injury.

"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said.

The French driver is eighth in the standings despite his absence. He's been consistent, placing in the top six in each of his last seven races, but has rarely been able to challenge four-time champion Verstappen's pace.

Mekies said Hadjar had been "superb on and off track" since moving up from Red Bull's sister team Racing Bulls after a strong rookie season in 2025, "which made extending his contract an easy decision".

That means Verstappen will have the same teammate for a second season, the first time that's happened since Sergio Perez was dropped at the end of 2024. Red Bull dropped Liam Lawson after two races in 2025 and Yuki Tsunoda replaced him but was dropped at the end of the year.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in (Red Bull headquarters at) Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me," Hadjar said.

articles.title: Steelers news: Ben Roethlisberger makes eye-opening take on DK Metcalf's issues
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are experiencing early offensive growing pains, and wide receiver DK Metcalf finds himself at the center of the frustration. Brought...
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are experiencing early offensive growing pains , and wide receiver DK Metcalf finds himself at the center of the frustration. Brought in as a marquee weapon for veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers , Metcalf has struggled to produce through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season.

Through two games, the star wideout has caught just eight passes on 19 targets for 67 yards and zero touchdowns. His hands became a major talking point during Pittsburgh's painful 20-3 Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots , where costly drops stalled an already sluggish offense. After managing a narrow 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1, the Steelers need their top target to elevate the passing attack.

While critics suggest extra practice reps , former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger has a very different view on Metcalf's early-season slump. Speaking on his "Footbahlin" podcast, the franchise legend offered an eye-opening assessment of the receiver's current state.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I don't think it's a lack of confidence; I think receivers are one of the most confident people in the world," Roethlisberger said. "I think people will say something like, does he need to catch more passes… No, it's not about reps. He's going to catch 98 to 99 of those 100 each time. Like it is what it is, he's got hands, he can catch."

Instead of physical mechanical issues, Big Ben believes Metcalf is simply overthinking and pressing too hard to break out of his slump. "Right now I think he's probably in his own head a little bit," Roethlisberger explained. "When you start to struggle, the issue is you start pressing too much, you start trying too hard… Just be you, and I'm hoping, I think he's a pro, Aaron's probably like hey listen, dude relax."

Roethlisberger's advice is clear: Metcalf must trust his proven track record and let the game come to him naturally.
